raw.text: EuO is a ferromagnetic europium chalcogenide and oxide material (10.1103/PhysRevLett.122.086401, 10.1088/2053-1583/aa6663) that serves as a ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1103/PhysRevB.102.155413, 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014443), a ferromagnetic insulator (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.1.062001, 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.125305, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b04509), a magnetic insulator (10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.116803), and a half-metallic semiconductor (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.124419). It is a Heisenberg ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.044404) and a strong Heisenberg ferromagnet with a magnetic moment of 7 mu_B/f.u. (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.9.064401). As a NaCl-structured magnetic oxide with large saturation magnetization and high Curie temperature (10.1021/acsami.0c05332), it is used as a ferromagnetic substrate (10.1103/PhysRevB.105.205436, 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.035115, 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014443), a magnetic substrate to induce magnetization in 2D materials (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.5.L022038), a magnetic substrate material (10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.056402), a magnetic europium oxide substrate (10.1021/acsami.7b11454), and a substrate material (10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L041402, 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L121302). It is also described as a ferromagnetic oxide material forming the heterostructure interface (10.1038/s41567-024-02443-x), a ferromagnetic material used in heterostructures (10.1002/adfm.202506394), a magnetic oxide component of the EuO-KTaO3 interface (10.1002/apxr.202200026), and a perovskite transition metal oxide used at the interface (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043231). Ferromagnetic EuO induces magnetism in the adjacent LTO buffer layer and the interfacial KTaO3 (KTO) (10.1002/adfm.202506394). It is a suitable candidate for material realization of stacked Chern insulators (10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c04304). The propagation length for non-equilibrium magnons in EuO has been determined (10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b04509). A giant spin-phonon interaction is present (10.1039/c9nr01931f). Direct EuO/Si contact holds high promise for spintronics (10.1002/adfm.202104925). It is also described as magnetic insulating EuO thin films (10.1002/adma.202417669), high-quality EuO (111) thin film (10.1038/s41535-022-00506-x), and a ferromagnetic insulator conducting for spin current but insulating for electric current (10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b04509).

raw.text: The twisted trilayer magnet (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_108_L100401_1) is a material system consisting of two-dimensional magnets with three layers twisted relative to each other (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L100401). It exhibits rich magnetic domain structures, which are stabilized by complex interlayer coupling effects in the moiré superlattice (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L100401). These domain structures can be significantly manipulated by adjusting the twist angle, and external magnetic fields can easily manipulate them as well (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L100401).

raw.text: CoI₂ is a cobalt-based van der Waals antiferromagnet (source: 10.1038/s41567-023-02180-7) and a multiferroic van der Waals material with helimagnetic order and electric polarization (source: 10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c01053), classified as a transition metal diiodide (XI₂ compound where X = Co; source: 10.1007/s10853-025-10972-w), a 2D metal dihalide with M = Co and X = I (source: 10.1021/acsnano.4c04397), a d-orbital-based metal ion compound forming nanoclusters (source: 10.1021/acsanm.4c05647), an emerging class of 2D magnet (source: 10.1021/acsnano.5c19196), a van der Waals triangular antiferromagnet (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5), a two-dimensional transition-metal dihalide (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.034001), an unconventional two-dimensional (2D) crystalline material (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539), and a buckled monolayer 2D transition metal halide (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1). CoI₂ and NiI₂ retain their ferromagnetic (FM) ground states under biaxial strains (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ade7c6), while the interlayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) to ferromagnetic (FM) transition has been observed in bilayer NiI₂ when the critical electron doping concentration reaches 0.625% (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.2c01479); CoI₂ exhibits a ferromagnetic (FM) state induced by electron doping (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.2c01479). The other compounds favor antiferromagnetic ordering (source: 10.1007/s10853-025-10972-w). Helimagnetic orders exist simultaneously with electric polarization in NiI₂ and CoI₂ (source: 10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c01053); below 60 K, an incommensurate magnetic reflection is observed which exhibits finite circular dichroism in RXS, signaling the inversion symmetry-breaking helimagnetic ground state, with q approximate to [0.143,0,1.49] reciprocal lattice units (source: 10.1002/adma.202417434). CoI₂ exhibits remarkable in-plane auxetic behavior with a negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1). CoI₂ exhibits a Curie temperature as high as 320 K (method: first-principles calculations; source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ade7c6). The easy magnetization axis lies in-plane for FeI₂ and CoI₂, and out-of-plane for NiI₂ (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ade7c6). MnBr₂, CoBr₂, and CoI₂ exhibit half-metallicity in the ferrimagnetic phase (source: 10.1007/s10853-025-10972-w). A peak at 55 K in the temperature-normalized heat capacity suggests the presence of entropy variation (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539). The experimental helical AF order in CoI₂ results from combined effects (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5). The high-spin Co²⁺ ion is in the Jeff = 1/2 state because of strong spin-orbit coupling (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5). All three monolayers (FeI₂, CoI₂, NiI₂) exhibit relatively large MAE values, with NiI₂ showing the largest (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ade7c6). Under pressure, the optical conductivity increases from 9900 to 11600 (Ω cm)⁻¹ (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539), and the refractive index increases from 2.75 to 3.5 (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539). CoI₂ was found to be a semiconductor with a band gap energy of 2.1 eV (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539). Due to large Coulomb interaction, U/W > 1 (with bandwidth W) in most TM halides, making them strongly correlated materials (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.034001). A strong Kitaev interaction (K1) at the first nearest neighbors (1NN) gives rise to the magnetic properties (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5). CoI₂ exhibits low thermal conductivity ranging from 5 to 0.1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129539). A weak Heisenberg interaction J1 is determined (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5), and the weak trigonal elongation and crystal field contribute to the observed weak in-plane magnetic anisotropy (source: 10.1103/c6r4-fgj5).

raw.name: MoX2
raw.text: MoX2 encompasses a wide range of two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials that exhibit ferromagnetism, including pristine VS2 nanosheets (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2017.01.192), 1T-VS2 monolayer (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c03109), monolayer VS2 with a saturation magnetization (M-s) of 37 emu per cc and coercivity (H-c) of 135 Oe at 300 K (source: 10.1002/adfm.202213295), VSe2 monolayer as a robust room-temperature ferromagnetic semiconductor under -2 to 4% strain (source: 10.1007/s10853-021-06311-4), VSe2 monolayer with room-temperature ferromagnetism (source: 10.1021/acsami.9b02493), monolayer VS2 and VSe2 as ferromagnetic (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/18/11/113038), VSe2 monolayer with a Curie point above 330 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085117), strong ferromagnetic ordering for monolayer VSe₂ (source: 10.1038/s41565-018-0063-9), monolayer VSe2 with Curie temperature above room temperature (source: 10.1007/s12274-022-4400-9), monolayer VSe2 without charge density waves as a ferromagnet with ordering temperature of 250 K (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ab8b48), and monolayers of VSe2 predicted to be ferromagnetic (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.235147); however, no signatures of ferromagnetic ordering were observed in monolayer VSe₂ in one study (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b01649). The material also includes CrI3 monolayer with ferromagnetic order below 45 K (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/aaf06d) and Curie temperature of 45 K (source: 10.1039/d2nr05342j), with estimates of 55-65 K (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ab72d8), and bulk CrI3 ferromagnetic at 61 K (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b04282); Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ (CGT) as a semiconducting 2D ferromagnet with out-of-plane magnetization (source: 10.1002/adma.201906021), pristine Curie temperature of 66 K enhanced to 240 K by Na intercalation (source: 10.1002/adma.202400270), and T_C1 ≈ 69 K (source: 10.1002/smll.202302240); Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with Curie temperature range 130-220 K (source: 10.1002/advs.202206842), bulk ferromagnetic transition at 205 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.014425), and thin crystals as metallic ferromagnets with easy axis perpendicular to layers (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b01278); Fe4GeTe2 as a nearly room-temperature vdW ferromagnet (source: 10.1103/wmb3-5r6b) with T-C = 68 K (source: 10.1038/s42005-022-00921-3); CrBr3 monolayer with Curie temperature of 34 K (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b00553); VTe2 monolayer with in-plane ferromagnetic ground state and Curie temperature of 377 K (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2020.148098); CrGeTe3 with Curie temperature TC ~ 66 K at ambient condition (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.217203); VI3 ferromagnetic at 49 K (source: 10.1002/adma.201808074) and 50 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.014105); Cr₂Te₃ with Curie temperature of 180 K (source: 10.1080/21663831.2020.1865469) and thickness-dependent Tc from 160 K in thick flakes to 280 K in 6 UC (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b05128); Fe5GeTe2 with high Curie temperature exceeding 300 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.045137) and paramagnetic to ferromagnetic transition at ~302 K (source: 10.3390/nano15010019); Cr5Te8 with Curie temperature above 220 K (source: 10.1021/acsnano.4c08700) and 176 K (source: 10.1021/acsami.3c02446); and CrCl3 as a prototype ferromagnetic honeycomb lattice material (source: 10.1016/j.actamat.2022.118390). The material also exhibits ferromagnetism in Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ bilayer and CrI₃ monolayer (source: 10.1063/5.0031870), and in Cr₂S₃ (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c05105), Cr₂Se₃ (source: 10.1021/acs.chemmater.3c00172), and Cr₂S₃ as a ferromagnetic insulator (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417396).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: PtSe2
raw.text: PtSe2 is a two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide (2D TMDC) with M = Pt and X = Se, also described as layered platinum diselenide, van der Waals 1T-PtSe2 thin films, and a centrosymmetric dichalcogenide monolayer (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084002; WOS:000864281600003; 10.1002/adma.202504964; 10.1016/j.commatsci.2025.114189). It is a semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide characterized by an indirect band gap, space inversion symmetry, and high carrier mobility (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.125409); intrinsic PtSe2 is a non-magnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/adfabd; 10.1088/1402-4896/ad2e58; 10.1103/PhysRevB.94.104426; 10.1002/advs.202103507), with monolayer PtSe2 exhibiting a bandgap of 1.8 eV (source: 10.1002/adfm.202110428) and a narrow bandgap (source: 10.1016/j.mseb.2025.118559). The material also displays tunable semiconducting to metallic phase transition (source: 10.1039/c6nr07975j), and exfoliated 2D layers are semiconductors (source: 10.1002/adma.202313511). PtSe2 exhibits strong interlayer interaction (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.144403), inherent strong hidden-spin spin-orbit coupling (SOC) enabling high-performance magnetic device operations from 0.3 K to room temperature (source: 10.1002/adma.202504964), and strong spin-orbit coupling (source: 10.1002/adma.202304243; 10.1063/5.0256072). It shows anisotropic Rashba-like spin splitting with highly anisotropic Rashba-like spin splittings in multiple Fermi surfaces (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.99.045438), and nonmonotonic band bending potential with an unusual nonmonotonic form with spatially segregated electron accumulation and hole accumulation regions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.99.045438). The material exhibits ferromagnetism, with both c-2H-PtSe2 and a-2H-PtSe2 showing butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis (method: magnetic transport; source: 10.1002/adfm.202308681), and transition metal doping (single atom of Fe or Mn and two atoms of Fe, Mn doped) successfully induces magnetic properties (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416493). Magnetoresistance studies reveal negative MR appears upon cooling (source: 10.1002/advs.202103507), and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations occur exclusively in plane at B >= 4.5 T (source: 10.1103/7dzw-wlpx). The material shows a thickness-dependent Kondo effect with metal to insulator transition and negative MR upon cooling (source: 10.1002/advs.202103507), and intrinsic spin Hall conductivity tunable from positive to negative values by changing the stacking mode (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.125403). Spin Hall conductivity is tunable via electric field modulation of Fermi level and Berry curvature (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c01363), and spin-to-charge conversion is tunable with number of layers, electric field, or strain (source: 10.1002/adma.202304243). PtSe2 also exhibits sliding ferroelectricity, with polarization shifting from left-oriented to right-oriented upon slippage (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/adf5dc). It is described as a multivalley semimetal (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.99.045438), an air-stable metallic transition metal dichalcogenide (source: 10.1021/accountsmr.1c00092), an air-stable type-II Dirac semimetal (source: 10.1002/adma.202005465), and a Dirac semimetal (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c01363). It is used as a component in heterostructures, including PtSe2/HfS2 van der Waals heterostructures (source: 10.1016/j.micrna.2025.208380), PtS2/PtSe2 van der Waals heterojunctions (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/adf9d8), and as a sliding ferroelectric barrier layer in van der Waals multiferroic tunnel junctions (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/adf5dc). It is also used as an electrode material (source: 10.1039/d4na00639a; 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c00440; 10.1088/0256-307X/42/7/070705), a symmetric electrode material (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/42/7/070705), and a material with small lattice mismatch and large spin-orbit torque (source: 10.1021/acsanm.5c00152). PtSe2 is a base material for the study of vacancy defects and doping (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416493), and is environment stable with Pt vacancy-induced magnetism (source: 10.1002/adfm.202308681). It is also noted as a component used to form an alloy with VSe₂ (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.1c00992), and as ultrathin metallic PtSe2 crystals (source: 10.1038/s41565-019-0467-1).

raw.name: FeSe
raw.text: FeSe is an iron-based compound and paramagnetic superconductor with the simplest structure (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/42/7/070714), studied as a layered van der Waals material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.174503), a 2D non-van der Waals semiconductor (source: 10.1002/adfm.202402080), a layered iron chalcogenide material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.125404), a two-dimensional topological insulator material (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.1c02069), a buckled monolayer 2D transition metal selenide (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1), and a well-known high-temperature 2D superconductor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.156406). It is a component of the superconducting alloy FeTe1-xSex (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.167001) and the base material system for ionic-liquid-gated (Li,Fe)OHFeSe (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.014504). FeSe exhibits paramagnetism (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/42/7/070714), an antiferromagnetic ground state with mixed single-stripe and block-checkerboard type antiferromagnetic ground states predicted (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2017.10.037), and a canted checkerboard antiferromagnetic (AFM) order in monolayer form (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00761-3). It also shows dimer texture spin ordering in monolayer FeSe (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.165424), and is a monolayer FeSe model representative of two-dimensional altermagnets (source: 10.1103/lh4w-byk7). The material exhibits 2D spin and orbital fluctuations that can be either that of a standard density wave or a topological vortex (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043154), Fermi surface nesting with (pi, pi) nesting between hole- and electron-like Fermi surface sheets (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2017.10.037), and d-band bandwidth renormalization where bandwidths are starkly overestimated at the generalized gradient approximation level and brought closer to experimentally observed values by introducing Hubbard U, Hund's J, or long-range magnetic orders (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043154). It shows remarkable in-plane auxetic behavior with a negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1), and a change in magnetic formation energy with local magnetic moment of Fe at a pressure up to 6 GPa (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043154). FeSe also demonstrates giant and reversible magnetic modulation involving On-Off ferromagnetic switching at high voltages and quasi-linear magnetization change at low voltages (source: 10.1002/adfm.202500234), and a nontrivial behavior of the spin-exchange parameters on the magnetization (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043154). It is a ferromagnetic system used for interlayer proximity effect (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2024.160850), and exhibits a quantum spin Hall edge state (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00761-3). FeSe is studied as nonsuperconducting FeSe thin films (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.035105), superconducting FeSe monolayers (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.165424), monolayer FeSe on Si(001) (source: 10.3390/nano12020270), monolayer FeSe on oxide substrates (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.115147), and monolayer FeSe on the anisotropic SrTiO3 (110) surface (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.94.045114). It is a layered material used as a base for intercalation studies (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.045145), a material system studied for 2D magnetic Dirac semimetal properties (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.186401), and a concrete material system studied using first-principles calculations (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.045118).

raw.name: Sc2CF2
raw.text: Sc2CF2 is a two-dimensional (2D) material belonging to the MXene family, specifically a semiconducting transition metal carbide (MXene) monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.152360; 10.1039/d2tc00246a; 10.1039/c7tc01765k; 10.1016/j.physb.2023.415124; 10.1039/c9tc01807g). It has been investigated as a base system for doping studies (source: 10.1016/j.ssi.2022.115983). The Sc2CF2 monolayer exhibits semiconductor character (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.152360). The calculated lowest Li diffusion barriers are 0.33 eV at 0 at%, 0.31 eV at 5 at%, 0.25 eV at 10 at%, and 0.23 eV at 20 at% N contents, determined via first-principles calculation (source: 10.1016/j.ssi.2022.115983). The first bright excitons of Sc- and Ti-based MXenes are strongly localized in k-space, as revealed by theoretical analysis (source: 10.1039/d2tc00246a). The optical gaps of Sc2CF2 lie in the energy region of visible light, with a reported value of 1.9–2.3 eV from time-dependent density functional theory with HSE06 hybrid functional (source: 10.1039/d2tc00246a).

complete valley-contrasting physics under time-reversal symmetry
effective time-reversal symmetry, which guarantees a strictly antisymmetric spin polarization of the electronic states
possessing both inversion asymmetry and time-reversal symmetry
Time reversal symmetry prevents magneto-optical effects in the absence of a magnetic field.
arising from time reversal symmetry

In TaIrTe4, applying a current parallel to the Berry curvature dipole results in out of plane orbital magnetization (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.035423). Additionally, TaIrTe4 exhibits unconventional spin-orbit torque with a large SOT effective field efficiency of the out-of-plane polarized spin current determined to be 0.37 (source: 10.1002/adma.202406464).

content.text: stable tetragonal phase of SnO2
intermediate nanolayer material
SnO2 host material for Cr doping
stable two-dimensional semiconductor

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: SnO2
raw.text: SnO2 is a stable tetragonal phase material (source: 10.3390/nano11071633) that serves as an intermediate nanolayer material (source: 10.1016/j.jpcs.2017.04.005) and as a host material for Cr doping (source: 10.1039/d5mh00937e). It is a stable two-dimensional semiconductor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.195408) and an indirect-gap semiconductor with a band gap in the region of 3.7 eV (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.195408). SnO2 exhibits an extremely high electron mobility, similar to 10^3 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.195408), and its band structure presents double Mexican-hat-like band edges in the valence bands near the Fermi level (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.195408).

raw.name: FePS3
raw.text: FePS3 (mat_10_1021_acsnano_5b05927_1) is a prototype van der Waals layered antiferromagnet under ambient conditions (10.21468/SciPostPhys.15.1.020), specifically a zig-zag-type intralayer antiferromagnet (10.1021/acsnano.4c12520) with a zigzag-type spin arrangement (10.1021/acsnano.5c12408). It is a two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnetic Mott insulator (10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.266801) and an antiferromagnetic insulator with compensated spin order (10.1039/d5mh00023h). The material exhibits antiferromagnetic order (10.1038/s41699-022-00315-7) with a Néel temperature T_N = 120 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L060403). Multiple transition temperatures have been reported: a transition from antiferromagnetic to paramagnetic phase at around 80 K (T_N1), a second magnetic phase transition at around 120 K (T_N2) due to two-dimensional spin critical fluctuations, and a transition at around 55 K (T_N3) associated with unbinding of spin vortices (10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b00758). An antiferromagnetic transition is also observed near ~78 K via electrical resistance variance (10.1063/1.5112130), and the noise spectral density increases strongly near T_N = 118 K (10.1002/aelm.202100408). The Néel temperature reduces with flake thickness (10.1021/acsnano.2c11654), but strong Néel ordering persists down to monolayer thickness (10.1002/lpor.202100431). ARPES measurements on an exfoliated FePS3 film at 6 K reveal its band structure in the antiferromagnetic phase (10.1088/2053-1583/add7ea). The best-fit exchange parameters are J(1) = -2.08 meV (ferromagnetic), J(2) = 0.26 meV, and J(3) = 4.21 meV (antiferromagnetic) for the nearest-, second-nearest, and third-nearest neighbors, respectively (10.1103/PhysRevB.102.184429). The intrinsic antiferromagnetic transition is observed in the FePS3 matrix (10.1039/d0qm00789g), and the material is a 2D layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1002/adma.202211653).

raw.text: CrN is a transition metal nitride (source: 10.1142/S0217979221503021) that exists as a two-dimensional multiferroic material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.056701), a 2D CrN system (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.235415), a monolayer CrN (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094441), a hexagonal CrN monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.physa.2023.128589), a two-dimensional ferromagnetic material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.075133), a magnetoelectric multiferroic material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.094418), a two-dimensional magnet with specific crystal symmetry (source: 10.1103/81rn-9t23), two-dimensional chromium nitride (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ade1b5), hexagonal chromium nitride (source: 10.1039/c6nr07790k), and pristine CrN (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.1c00774). It is also studied as a real material with rock-salt structure (source: 10.1103/gj66-4yhj), in epitaxial growth on GaN (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.150637), as CrN subdomains (source: 10.1002/adma.202304946), and as hexagonal CrN nanoribbons (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.205418). Pristine CrN shows an antiferromagnetic (AFM) behavior (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.1c00774), and exhibits a magnetostructural transition to an orthorhombically distorted phase below TN = 287 K, leading to a stable double-layered AFM order (source: 10.1103/gj66-4yhj). The magnon spectrum and temperature evolution of ordered magnetic moments are derived based on ab initio calculated exchange parameters (source: 10.1103/gj66-4yhj). As a 2D multiferroic, CrN possesses vertical electric polarization and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.220409), and exhibits consequential voltage-controlled reversal of DMI chirality in multiferroics (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.056701), as well as switching of a perpendicular magnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.056701).

raw.name: Graphene
raw.text: Graphene exhibits ferromagnetism as a property, with the following reported behaviors and values: At finite doping away from half filling, ferromagnetism is completely absent (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.95.104402). A phase transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases is observed in impurity-dependent magnetic susceptibility curves (source: 10.1088/0253-6102/67/5/569). Graphene exhibits an interplay of competing many-body instabilities, namely, s-wave superconductivity, ferromagnetism, and spin- and charge-density waves (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.95.035137). Ferromagnetism is observed in a two-dimensional electron system (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/ab4729). Ferromagnetically ordered phases are reported (source: 10.1103/pqq5-3n84). Highly spin-polarized electron transmission arises in junctions when the two edges of the center ZGNR are in the ferromagnetic configuration (source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2018.12.035). Twisted bilayer graphene exhibits ferromagnetism depending on the twist angle (source: 10.1016/j.eml.2022.101829). Saturated ferromagnetic (spin- and valley-polarized) states are ideal ground-state candidates at filling fractions +/- 3/4 in the large band-gap limit (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.235123). Untwisted heterobilayers of ferromagnetic van der Waals materials are studied (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.L100406). 58 ferromagnets are identified (source: 10.1038/s41524-024-01318-2). Exotic 2D materials and heterojunctions with desired properties for applications such as ferromagnetic (ferroelectric) tunnel junctions are identified (source: 10.1021/accountsmr.1c00246). Competing phases include ferromagnetic states depending on the values of Ising or XY anisotropies (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.075203). The moiré potential leads to a strong suppression of the ferromagnetism of the underlying metal (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.165122). A two-orbital spin-fermion model is established to describe ferromagnetism in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice, with Tc reaching a maximum at the quarter-filled case and a linear relationship between Tc and doping concentration in other regions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.094401). A ferromagnetic ground state is found near a particular electron density and for a range of effective electron (or hole) masses (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.086501). Ferromagnetism is present in all three directions for the frustrated triangular lattice at half-filling (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.415902). Three distinct phases are classified: ferromagnet, skyrmion, and mixed phase (source: 10.1103/55z5-cm5q).

raw.text: V2C is a V-based bare MXene (carbide) and a two-dimensional transition metal monocarbide (2D MXene) with M=V (source: 10.1016/j.mtcomm.2022.103875, 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669); it is also described as a layered transition metal monocarbide (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.195129), a Janus V2C (source: 10.1021/acsnano.8b09201), a two-dimensional (2D) material (source: 10.1021/acsami.1c07906), and an MXene used for comparison of Li capacity (source: 10.1016/j.ssi.2022.115983). Monolayer V₂C is a metal with unstable antiferromagnetism but is stable according to calculated formation energy and phonon spectrum (source: 10.1039/c6nr01333c). V2C stabilizes in an antiferromagnetic configuration with a sizeable magnetic moment exceeding 2.0 mu_B, prefers C-type antiferromagnetic ordering, has an in-plane easy axis, and a small magnetic anisotropy energy (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669). The Neel temperature of V2N is calculated to be ~335 K (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669). d bands crossing near the Fermi level (EF) induce multiple nodal lines (NLs) in bulk M2C and multiple nodal points (NPs) in few-layered M2C (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.195129). The inclusion of spin-orbit coupling breaks the degeneracy of NLs and NPs, contributing to large spin Hall conductivity (SHC) up to ~1100 (h/e)(Ω cm)⁻¹ for bulk Ta₂C, up to ~200 (h/e)(Ω cm)⁻¹ for monolayer Ta₂C, and up to ~600 (h/e)(Ω cm)⁻¹ for eight-layer Ta₂C (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.195129).

raw.text: V2N is a V-based bare MXene (nitride) (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669). Monolayer V₂N is a nonmagnetic metal (source: 10.1039/c6nr01333c) and is stable according to calculated formation energy and phonon spectrum (source: 10.1039/c6nr01333c). However, V2N stabilizes in an antiferromagnetic configuration with a sizeable magnetic moment exceeding 2.0 μB (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669), specifically preferring A-type antiferromagnetic ordering (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669). It exhibits large magnetic anisotropy (~100 μeV/atom) (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669) and an out-of-plane easy axis (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669). The Neel temperature of V2N is calculated to be ~335 K (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417669).

content.text: novel two-dimensional S = 1/2 antiferromagnet with randomly depleted square lattice

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: LiCu3O3
raw.text: LiCu3O3 is a novel two-dimensional S = 1/2 antiferromagnet with a randomly depleted square lattice (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.115151). It exhibits antiferromagnetic order with magnetic order occurring at Tc1 = 123 K and a change in the magnetic state at Tc2 ≈ 30 K, as determined by magnetization measurements (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.115151). The material possesses a rigid magnetic structure, evidenced by relatively small magnetic susceptibility at all orientations of the applied magnetic field, with an estimated saturation field of μ0Hsat ≈ 200 T derived from differential susceptibility measured at μ0H = 5 T (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.115151). Its magnetic behavior is typical of a spiral spin structure, characteristic of spiral, spin-modulated magnetic structures or structures with frozen disorder (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.115151). Additionally, a spin-flop transition indicates weak uniaxial anisotropy of the spin structure (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.115151).

raw.name: CrI3
raw.text: CrI3 is a prototypical van der Waals ferromagnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.094415) and a two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic (FM) semiconductor (source: 10.1039/d2nr05342j). Bulk CrI3 is ferromagnetic with a Curie temperature of 61 K (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b04282; 10.1103/PhysRevX.8.041028; 10.1103/PhysRevX.11.031047; 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.115148). The CrI3 monolayer exhibits long-range ferromagnetic order with a Curie temperature of approximately 45 K (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858; 10.1088/2053-1583/aaf06d; 10.1039/d2nr05342j; 10.1088/2053-1583/aa75ed; 10.1038/s41535-024-00666-y), while other estimates yield 55–65 K (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ab72d8) or 46 K (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129994). The monolayer remains FM with T-C ~75 K (source: 10.1209/0295-5075/114/47001). The material exhibits ferromagnetic order with out-of-plane easy axis in monolayer CrI₃ (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2020.109820) and possesses the ferromagnetic nature of out-of-plane Ising spin-up electrons (source: 10.1016/j.mtadv.2024.100525). Monolayer CrI₃ is a prototypical vdW ferromagnet where isotropic exchange interactions govern magnetic long-range order in the undoped system (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ae1512). The material exhibits ferromagnetic order maintained upon exfoliating bulk crystals down to a single layer (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.014420). In bilayer CrI₃, pressure induces a transition from layered antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase; in trilayer CrI₃, pressure can create coexisting domains of three phases, one ferromagnetic and two antiferromagnetic (source: 10.1038/s41563-019-0505-2). Bilayer CrI₃ can be efficiently switched between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic types (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00706-w). Various van der Waals functionals unequivocally point to the ferromagnetic ground state for the low-temperature structured bilayer CrI₃ (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.031001). The material exhibits ferromagnetic intralayer order (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.085414). A remarkable fivefold increase in the ferromagnetic Curie temperature is predicted in monolayer CrI₃ within experimentally obtainable hole density (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.214411). Li adsorption can dramatically enhance its ferromagnetism (source: 10.1016/j.physleta.2020.126754). Chlorination can increase the Curie temperature up to 204 K (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129994). Surface I vacancies enhance the intrinsic ferromagnetism of monolayer CrI3 (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b00314). When compressive and tensile strains were applied, CrI3 remains ferromagnetic (source: 10.1016/j.mseb.2023.116409). The stabilization of ferromagnetism is attributable to orbital mixing between I p and Cr eg states, and to the presence of strong Hund's coupling (source: 10.1103/bdbj-98tj). The ferromagnetically ordered state is destroyed above 22 GPa (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L081104). The material ideally orders ferromagnetically on cooling from a monoclinic to a rhombohedral phase (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.024409).

content.text: a two-dimensional square-lattice compound with rare-earth magnetic Yb3+ ions

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: Bi2YbO4Cl
raw.text: Bi2YbO4Cl is a two-dimensional square-lattice compound with rare-earth magnetic Yb3+ ions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.075128). From the fit to the Curie-Weiss law on the magnetic susceptibility data in the low-temperature region, the observed Curie-Weiss temperature is about -1 K, implying an antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling between the Yb3+ moments (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.075128). Total energy calculations suggest an easy-axis (out-of-plane) anisotropy of the spins (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.075128). Magnetization and heat capacity data analysis confirms that the Yb3+ ion hosts the spin-orbit driven Jeff = 1/2 state at low temperatures (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.075128). Heat capacity data show the presence of a broad maximum at 0.3 K and the absence of any sharp magnetic anomaly down to 0.09 K, indicating the onset of short-range correlations (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.075128).

content.text: A two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric topological superconductor

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: superconducting antiferromagnetic quantum spin Hall insulator
raw.text: The material is a superconducting antiferromagnetic quantum spin Hall insulator, described as a two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric topological superconductor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.081412). It exhibits an e(2)/h conductance, which is a quantized conductance (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.081412). It possesses a helical Majorana edge mode, specifically a Kramers pair of two chiral Majorana edge modes in opposite propagating directions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.081412). Additionally, it hosts a helical electron edge mode (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.081412).

raw.name: VSSe
raw.text: VSSe is a two-dimensional Janus monolayer van der Waals compound and transition-metal dichalcogenide, described as a Janus vanadium-dichalcogenide monolayer, a 2D intrinsic ferromagnetic semiconductor, and a room-temperature ferromagnetic Janus monolayer (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b05050). It exhibits a Curie temperature of 300 K as predicted by Monte Carlo simulations based on the Ising model (source: 10.1016/j.micrna.2023.207537). The in-plane magnetic anisotropy energy of VSSe reaches up to 0.74 meV per cell in the absence of strain (source: 10.1016/j.micrna.2023.207537). VSSe demonstrates intrinsic ferroelasticity via a strain-driven 90-degree lattice rotation with an extremely high reversal strain of 73% (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b05050). Its low symmetry C-3v point group results in giant in-plane piezoelectric polarization (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b05050). Additionally, VSSe exhibits electric-field-induced topological magnetism as a result of tunable in-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (source: 10.1039/d5tc00444f).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: Cr2Ge2Te6
raw.text: Cr2Ge2Te6 (CGT) is a semiconducting 2D ferromagnet with out-of-plane magnetization (source: 10.1002/adma.201906021), described as a rare layered ferromagnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2020.412344) and a van der Waals ferromagnet (source: 10.1039/d0nr06054b). The pristine material exhibits ferromagnetic order with a Curie temperature of 66 K (source: 10.1002/adma.202400270), while other reports give T_C1 ≈ 69 K (source: 10.1002/smll.202302240) and a Curie temperature determined from electrical transport measurements of approximately 40 K (source: 10.1002/aelm.202101383). The critical properties of single-crystalline Cr2Ge2Te6 were investigated by bulk dc magnetization around the paramagnetic to ferromagnetic phase transition (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.054406), and the phase diagrams of Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ and Cr₂Si₂Te₆ disclose a triple point around the Curie temperature (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.134417). The material exhibits ferromagnetic order maintained upon exfoliating the bulk down to a few layers (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.214420), capable of retaining long-range ferromagnetic order even in its monolayer form (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.153368), and shows ferromagnetic ordering at the two-dimensional limit (source: 10.1002/advs.202302444). The magnetic ground state of monolayer CGT is FM (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416721). Strong enhancement of ferromagnetism in Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ has been reported (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c00201), and moderate in-plane strain is sufficient to strongly enhance ferromagnetism up to room temperature (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.L022040). Na intercalation enhances TC to 240 K (source: 10.1002/adma.202400270), and exposure to air results in advent of a stable nonlayered secondary ferromagnetic phase Cr₂Te₃ with T_C2 ≈ 160 K (source: 10.1002/smll.202302240). The in-plane and out-of-plane resonance fields of CGT gradually merge into a same field as the temperature rises to Curie Temperature, indicating changes of anisotropy (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2022.167401). Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ acts as a ferromagnetic tunnel barrier with anisotropic magnetic moments (source: 10.1002/adma.202314190), and magnetic orientation of CGT can be detected accurately (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c02965). The material is a 2D ferromagnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.196402) with a Curie temperature matching the AHE hysteresis loops persisting to approximately 60 K (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b05121). Micro-area Kerr measurements demonstrate bipolar tunable magnetization loops below the Curie temperature (source: 10.1038/s41565-018-0186-z). The adsorption of molecules can effectively enhance the ferromagnetism and Curie temperature of the CGT sheet (source: 10.1039/c8tc05530k).

raw.name: CrSiTe3
raw.text: CrSiTe3 is a ferromagnetic van der Waals material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.144525) that exhibits intrinsic ferromagnetic order in the atomically thin limit (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.047203) and is capable of retaining long-range ferromagnetic order even in its monolayer form (source: 10.1002/lpor.202000025). The material shows a single-domain and out-of-plane magnetization for the thinnest films (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ac7b96). Below the Curie temperature of 34 K, the material retains ferromagnetic ordering (source: 10.1002/adma.202514083), with evidence of incipient antiferromagnetism below 1 kOe concomitant to ferromagnetic order at 33 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.L100407). The observed behavior is consistent with the presence of previously reported short-range magnetic order (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.104306). Enhancement of ferromagnetism, usually competing for orders, has been observed in CrSiTe3 at high pressure (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.3c00507). The magnetic ground state of monolayer CST and CSS is FM (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416721). The phase diagrams of Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ and Cr₂Si₂Te₆ disclose a triple point around the Curie temperature (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.134417). Stabilizing the finite-temperature ferromagnetism in the two-dimensional compound CrSiTe3 has been reported (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.214425).

raw.text: Magnets (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_103_184421_1) are generic magnetic materials capable of hosting spin helices and topological textures (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.184421). They exhibit a spin helix superposition property, where a superposition of spin helices can yield topological spin textures, such as skyrmion and hedgehog lattices (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.184421).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: λ-(BETS)2FeCl4
raw.text: λ-(BETS)2FeCl4 is a quasi-two-dimensional organic conductor and pi-d system that exhibits an antiferromagnetic insulating (AFI) phase below ~8.5 K (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.044601), with the antiferromagnetic order of the pi spins (not the Fe 3d spins) in the AFI phase (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.86.014702). It undergoes a spin-flop transition at ~1.2 T, observed as a very sharp structure (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.86.014702) or a sharp structure (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.044601), and an antiferromagnetic insulator-paramagnetic metal (AFI-PM) transition at ~10 T, seen as a step-like behavior with small hysteresis (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.86.014702) or a step at ~10 T (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.044601). The magnetocaloric effect (MCE) shows a small sharp peak at the spin-flop transition, a sharp dip at the AFI-PM transition (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.044601), and a broad dip at ~5 T below ~3 K (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.044601). The material also undergoes a field-induced superconducting transition (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.165115). The effective interaction between pi electrons via d spins drives an antiferromagnetic transition at a finite transition temperature Tc (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.88.043001), and the antiferromagnetic transition temperature T-N and sublattice magnetizations m(T) (for small/pi spins) and M(T) (for large/d spins) are derived as functions of temperature (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.043702). The sublattice magnetization m of pi electrons is almost constant at temperatures below approximately 0.95Tc (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.88.043001), and when T increases, m(T) is constant with a slight decrease below T-N, while M(T) decreases significantly (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.87.043702). Critical exponents below Tc are obtained as alpha = 3/4, beta = 1/8, gamma = 1, delta = 9, psi = 1/5, and nu = 5/8 (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.89.043001), with beta(1) = 1/8 for pi spins (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.89.043001). The effective Hamiltonian for the pi spins is reduced to the two-dimensional Ising model in the vicinity of Tc (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.89.043001), and the theory elucidates a novel mechanism for the first-order transition observed in this material (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.88.043001), explaining the extremely sharp peak of specific heat around Tc (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.88.043001).

content.text: layered ZrSiS-type structure compound

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: ZnVSb
raw.text: ZnVSb is a layered ZrSiS-type structure compound (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). Analysis of the heat capacity with both an ab initio perspective and Debye-Einstein model revealed a sizable anharmonic contribution to heat capacity, in line with the disordered nature of the material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). The experimental heat capacity reflected this feature by a boson peak with an Einstein temperature of 116 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). Ab initio phonon calculations show the formation of a collective phonon mode at 2.8 THz (134 K) (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). The bonding V-V distance is below the critical separation of 2.97 angstrom known from the literature, which allows for V-V orbital overlap and subsequent metallic conductivity (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). In ZnVSb, itinerant charge carriers coexist with a small, localized magnetic moment of ca. 0.25 mu(B) (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002); the concentration of itinerant charge carriers drops with decreasing temperature below 160 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). The susceptibility and electrical resistivity showed a large hysteresis between 120 K and 160 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002). This observation together with the overall shape of the hysteresis in the resistivity allows for suggesting a plausible origin of the effect as a charge-transfer metal-insulator transition occurring between 120 K and 160 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.015002).

raw.name: SnS2
raw.text: SnS₂ is a member of the layered metal dichalcogenides family (10.1016/j.apsusc.2020.146977) and a van der Waals (vdW) layered semiconductor (10.1063/5.0048885). It exhibits a hexagonal phase (10.1016/j.apsusc.2020.146977) indexed to the P3m1 space group (10.1016/j.mseb.2025.118929) and is a 2H-transition metal dichalcogenide (10.1063/5.0284570). The material is a nonmagnetic indirect band gap semiconductor both in bulk and in the monolayer limit (10.1103/PhysRevB.105.195205), with pure diamagnetic behavior (10.1088/1674-4926/43/9/092501; 10.1021/acsami.2c06797). Monolayer SnS₂ can be easily synthesized by cleaving its bulk crystal (10.1016/j.apsusc.2016.07.150). As a base material for monolayer systems (10.1016/j.physleta.2019.01.008; 10.1016/j.physleta.2017.03.034), it is used as a high on/off ratio transistor, photocatalyst, and electrode material (10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c00488). It also serves as a component of SnS₂/MnPSe₃/SnS₂ heterostructures (10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c02248), a van der Waals homobilayer host material (10.1021/acsnano.3c08117), and a layered intermediate used in flux transformation (10.1002/adma.202509261). For SnS (tin monosulfide), it is a group-IV monochalcogenide (10.1088/2053-1583/ab0146) with a buckled honeycomb monolayer structure (10.1039/d3ma01032e) and a rectangular unit cell (10.1103/wcbz-lbr1). Pristine 2D SnS is non-magnetic and semiconducting (10.1016/j.mssp.2022.107049; 10.3390/nano8100789), with MMA weakly adsorbed on its surface (10.1016/j.micrna.2026.208657). DFT calculations show energy gaps of 2.31 eV (PBE) and 3.01 eV (HSE06) for SnS, and 2.21 eV (PBE) and 2.88 eV (HSE06) for SnSe (10.1039/d3ma01032e). Giant intrinsic spin Hall conductivities (SHC) have been revealed in these materials (10.1088/2053-1583/ab0146). Upon Al doping, the band gap of 2D SnS reduces from 1.60 to 0.54 eV due to defect-level states, and the Al atom turns the nonmagnetic SnS nanosheet magnetic with a net magnetic moment of 0.32 μB, mainly from the spin-polarized p orbital of Al (10.1016/j.micrna.2026.208657). Chemical adsorption of MMA occurs on Al-SnS via an Al-O bridge (10.1016/j.micrna.2026.208657). Mn doping at up to 5 at% introduces two ferromagnetic phases with a canted spin direction (10.1002/adfm.202102560). TM doping elements significantly modify the optical properties of the AA-SnS₂ bilayer (10.1016/j.surfin.2021.101545). Both dopants retain the semiconductor nature of monolayer SnS with a tuneable band gap (10.1088/1402-4896/ac0375).

raw.text: ZnS is a semiconductor material that has been studied in various forms, including as a pristine monolayer, a 2D graphene-based structure, a candidate wurtzite monolayer semiconductor, a semiconductor shell material, a bulk counterpart proposed as a new class of hexagonal buckled monolayer, a polarized ZnS(0001) surface used as a substrate, and as the base material for the delta-(Zn,Cr)S diluted magnetic semiconductor (sources: 10.1016/j.physleta.2023.129042, 10.1007/s10853-017-1198-z, 10.1038/s41524-022-00740-8, 10.1021/acs.chemmater.9b00006, 10.1021/acsami.1c09267, 10.1021/acs.jpclett.7b02507, 10.1016/j.physb.2018.07.003). It is also classified as an M2X2 compound with M=Zn and X=S (source: 10.1103/c2qq-vc5f). ZnS exhibits direct band gap semiconducting behavior: the pristine monolayer ZnS is a semiconductor with a direct band gap (source: 10.1016/j.physleta.2023.129042), and ZnS GB is a semiconductor with a direct band gap of 3.4 eV in the I direction (source: 10.1007/s10853-017-1198-z). As an M2X2 compound, ZnS is a direct band-gap semiconductor with band gaps between 0.9 to 2.6 eV by DFT+Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof calculations and 1.3 to 3.7 eV by hybrid functional HSE calculations (source: 10.1103/c2qq-vc5f). Additionally, ZnS possesses direct bandgaps (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00740-8). ZnS also harbors strongly coupled ferroelectricity and ferroelasticity, possesses low cleavage energy, a giant in-plane negative Poisson's ratio, giant Rashba spin splitting, and an inherent self-healable capacity (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00740-8).

raw.name: ZnCu3(OH)6Cl2
raw.text: ZnCu3(OH)6Cl2 (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_97_104401_1) is a layered Mott insulator closely realizing the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model on the kagome lattice, described as an archetypal kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet and an archetype of a S = 1/2 nearest-neighbor Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the kagome lattice (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.104401; 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.L220406; 10.21468/SciPostPhysCore.8.4.092). It exhibits anisotropic exchange interactions, where the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction has an in-plane component almost three times larger than the out-of-plane component (source: 10.21468/SciPostPhysCore.8.4.092). The material shows diamond valence bond crystal order with a 12-site unit cell, resulting from a competition between a Z(2) spin liquid and a diamond valence bond crystal (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.104401). It also displays ferromagnetic coupling with impurities, where extra-plane magnetic impurities have a strong ferromagnetic interaction approximately one third of the main exchange J1 with the kagome magnetic sites (source: 10.21468/SciPostPhysCore.8.4.092). The debate on its quantum spin liquid behavior remains open, considering either a Z(2) spin liquid with very short-range correlations (some kind of resonating valence bond spin liquid) or an algebraic spin liquid with power-law correlations (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.104401).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: LuMnO3
raw.text: LuMnO3 is a two-dimensional multiferroic compound, an insulating 2D triangular-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevB.98.134412, 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.134444), and a representative material belonging to the orthorhombic space group (10.1039/d3nr03681b). It is a perovskite manganite material (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.241112) and an antiferromagnetic perovskite (10.1007/s10853-022-08000-2), also described as a ferromagnetic LaMnO3 insulator (10.1002/adma.201805970) and an antiferromagnetic manganite epitaxial thin film (10.1002/aelm.201800055). As an oxide film, it can be grown in ultrathin films down to the monolayer limit (10.1016/j.actamat.2026.122142) and is used as an epitaxial film of LaMnO3 (10.1021/acsami.4c14945) and as a ferromagnetic thin film material in heterostructures (10.1002/smll.202106029). It is also a perovskite oxide component in superlattices (10.1021/acsami.0c10579) and a component of the LuyY1-yMnO3 system (10.1103/PhysRevB.107.214407). LuMnO3 exhibits altermagnetism, where the altermagnetism influences the electronic states allowing the presence of non-relativistic spin-splittings along specific k-paths of the 3D Brillouin zone (10.1039/d3nr03681b), with a spin splitting of ~0.8 eV (10.1103/twhq-32db). It also exhibits ferromagnetism: the appearance of spontaneous magnetization strongly depends on the fluctuations of order parameters and the magnetoelectric coupling, occurring during the transition from paramagnetic to ferromagnetic phase (10.1016/j.physleta.2021.127305); despite its strong ferromagnetic properties, LaMnO3 is hindered by a high number of oxygen defects (10.1002/smll.202405734). Additionally, it exhibits biaxial magnetic anisotropy, with typical 4-fold biaxial magnetic anisotropy in biaxially strained epitaxial thin films (10.1021/acsami.4c14945). It exhibits ferroelectricity, where the appearance of spontaneous polarization strongly depends on the fluctuations of order parameters and the magnetoelectric coupling, occurring during the transition from paraelectric to ferroelectric phase (10.1016/j.physleta.2021.127305). The material also has a short lifetime when employed in electronic memory devices (10.1002/smll.202405734).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: MnTe
raw.text: MnTe (manganese telluride) is a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic manganese chalcogenide and a leading altermagnetic candidate with a layered antiferromagnetic structure, high Néel temperature (TN ≈ 310 K, source: 10.1002/adfm.202405829; also reported as ~300 K, source: 10.1103/twhq-32db; and T_N ~ 160 K, source: 10.1039/d1nr00822f), and semiconducting properties. Its pristine form prefers antiferromagnetic order (source: 10.1021/acsanm.8b01642), and bulk MnTe exhibits antiferromagnetic behavior (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ace635). α-MnTe is a room-temperature antiferromagnetic, direct band gap p-type semiconductor with unique energy band structure (source: 10.1021/acs.chemmater.0c03898). MnTe exhibits altermagnetic order with large electrically switchable spin splitting (~0.8 eV, source: 10.1103/twhq-32db), and the altermagnetism influences electronic states allowing non-relativistic spin-splittings along specific k-paths of the 3D Brillouin zone (source: 10.1039/d3nr03681b). Electronic transport and in situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy show the films are natively metallic with the Fermi level in the valence band (source: 10.1002/adfm.202405829). Neutron diffraction confirms the film is antiferromagnetic with planar anisotropy (source: 10.1002/adfm.202405829). The band structure is in good agreement with first-principles calculations for altermagnetic spin-splitting (source: 10.1002/adfm.202405829). MnTe exhibits fractional quantum ferroelectricity where polarization can be reversed (source: 10.1103/twhq-32db). Strong magnetoelectric coupling is naturally realized in the proposed fractional quantum multiferroic state, coupling fractional quantum ferroelectricity with altermagnetism (source: 10.1103/twhq-32db). Pristine MnX and their Janus counterparts are indirect-gap semiconductors (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085410). These materials have robust AFM order, retaining a much lower energy than the FM state even under strain (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085410). MnTe is a canonical altermagnet (source: 10.1002/adfm.202516924), a bulk candidate material for fractional quantum multiferroics (source: 10.1103/twhq-32db), a representative material belonging to the hexagonal space group (source: 10.1039/d3nr03681b), and a pristine form of manganese(II) telluride (source: 10.1021/acsanm.8b01642). It is also a component of the MnTe-Bi2Te3 system (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.03.030), the MnTe-SnTe-Bi2Te3 pseudo-ternary system (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2026.132365), a dilute magnetic semiconductor component (source: 10.1038/s41567-024-02477-1), a multiferroic superlattice component forming interface with GeTe (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c02584), an antiferromagnetic material used for interface coupling (source: 10.1038/s41699-017-0033-3), a layered Mn-Te compound (source: 10.1021/acsanm.5c02678), a competing binary phase in the synthesis reaction of MnBi₂Te₄ (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00427-y), a transition-metal fluoride altermagnet (source: 10.1103/r7mn-yklk), an altermagnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1103/4dpl-ptd9), a precursor material in phase transition (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c00956), a stoichiometric transition metal dichalcogenide atomic chain with M=Mn (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c), a transition metal dichalcogenide with magnetic transition metal element Mn (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.024414), and an antiferromagnetic insulator (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.115152). Single-crystalline γ-MnTe thin films with zinc-blende structure have been reported (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.155733). MnX2 chains are antiferromagnetic semiconductors (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c) and can be converted to half metals via carrier doping, exhibiting antiferromagnetic or ferromagnetic half metallicity depending on injected carrier type and concentration (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c). MX2 atomic chains are lattice-dynamically stable, confirmed from phonon spectra and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c). There is evidence of thickness-dependent transitions in magnetic ordering and anisotropy (source: 10.1016/j.mtchem.2024.102134), and intriguing topological and magnetic properties (source: 10.1021/acsanm.5c02678).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: RuO2
raw.text: RuO2 is a 4d transition metal oxide with half-filled d orbitals (source: 10.1016/j.cocom.2021.e00614) and a representative material belonging to the tetragonal space group (source: 10.1039/d3nr03681b). It is an unconventional magnet that exhibits a relatively high superconducting temperature in the thin film limit under applied strain (source: 10.1103/whm1-76jc). Using experimentally realistic parameters for RuO2, the Faraday angle is estimated in the absence of magnetic fields (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.024425). The charge response is investigated by computing the full optical conductivity tensor with and without magnetic field (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.024425). Additionally, RuO2 exhibits altermagnetic order with large electrically switchable spin splitting of ~0.8 eV (source: 10.1103/twhq-32db), and the altermagnetism influences the electronic states allowing the presence of non-relativistic spin-splittings along specific k-paths of the 3D Brillouin zone (source: 10.1039/d3nr03681b).

content.text: Hybrid systems represent one of the frontiers in the study of unconventional superconductivity
2D superconductor/ferromagnet system

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: superconductor-ferromagnet bilayer
raw.text: The superconductor-ferromagnet bilayer (mat_10_1038_s41567-024-02613_x) is a hybrid system representing a frontier in the study of unconventional superconductivity, specifically a 2D superconductor/ferromagnet system (source: 10.1038/s41567-024-02613-x; 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.144521). It exhibits a proximity-induced superfluid density that is two-fold anisotropic within the plane of the sample and shows power-law temperature scaling indicative of a nodal superconducting state (source: 10.1038/s41567-024-02613-x). The material also demonstrates a diode effect related to the manifestation of the diode effect in superconducting systems with spin-orbit interaction (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.144521). It hosts a helical superconducting state nucleated by a spin-splitting field and weak Rashba spin-orbit coupling (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.144521). A magnetoelectric effect is observed, allowing control of magnetization using the transport supercurrent in both dc and quasistatic ac regimes (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.144521). Modifications to the microwave response at frequencies near the ferromagnetic resonance suggest coupling between spin dynamics and induced superconducting order (source: 10.1038/s41567-024-02613-x). These properties are consistent with induced triplet p-wave pairing featuring a nodal p-wave order parameter (source: 10.1038/s41567-024-02613-x).

content.text: two dimensional misfit metallic compound
thermoelectric layered cobaltite single crystals

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: [Ca2CoO3]0.62[CoO2]
raw.text: [Ca2CoO3]0.62[CoO2] is a two-dimensional misfit metallic compound and thermoelectric layered cobaltite single crystal. It exhibits a metal-insulator transition (MIT) at intermediate temperature (~100 K) and enters a low-temperature spin density wave (SDW) phase below T-MIT, which becomes long range at 27 K. The material also shows exchange bias (EB) effects, glassiness, and a high-temperature spin-state transition. Additionally, it exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature variation of electrical resistivity and the Seebeck coefficient owing to the complex electronic and magnetic states (sources: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.094428, 10.1103/q6tk-52dc).

raw.name: CeSiI
raw.text: CeSiI is an intrinsic two-dimensional van der Waals heavy-fermion material (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c00619) and a van der Waals antiferromagnet and heavy-fermion metal (source: 10.1103/9ny7-qxyn), described as a van der Waals layered heavy fermion antiferromagnetic metal (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c05920), a van der Waals material exhibiting heavy fermion behavior and spiral order (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094404), a two-dimensional van der Waals heavy-fermion candidate (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00357-x), a van der Waals coupled material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.L121401), and a van der Waals material with Ce sites arranged on two layers of triangular lattices above and below the silicene layer (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.L201118). CeSiI exhibits both heavy fermion behavior and antiferromagnetic ordering (sources: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c05920, 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094404), with zero-field out of plane and in-plane electronic transport measurements indicating a heavy-fermion behavior with T2-linear dependence on resistivity in the antiferromagnetic state (source: 10.1103/9ny7-qxyn). It also exhibits spiral order and strong magnetic anisotropy (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094404). Resistivity and magnetometry measurements confirm the coexistence of itinerant electrons with magnetism with dominant antiferromagnetic exchange between the strongly Ising-like Ce moments below 7 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.L121401). Neutron diffraction confirms magnetic order with an incommensurate propagation vector k similar to (0.28, 0, 0.19) at 1.6 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.L121401). The vdW compound CeSiI hosts itinerant electrons coexisting with exotic magnetism (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.L121401). The Kondo resonance state of CeSiI does not change upon exfoliation and is an intrinsic property that persists upon exfoliation (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00357-x). Magnetic torque and magnetoresistance measurements reveal two metamagnetic transitions at mu_0H approximate to 2.4 and 4.2 T (source: 10.1103/9ny7-qxyn). The ground state of the monolayer can exhibit a nonmagnetic nematic heavy fermion phase that breaks C6 rotational symmetry for a small Heisenberg exchange (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.L201118). The quantum critical point can be identified by external perturbations in CeSiI (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00357-x). The Kondo resonance state can be easily controlled by strain and by surface doping (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00357-x). The presence of a two-step magnetic-field-induced phase transition along the c axis further suggests magnetic frustration in the ground state (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.L121401). CeSiI is established as the first intrinsic two-dimensional van der Waals heavy-fermion material up to 85 K (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c00619).

raw.name: Rashba ferromagnet
raw.text: The Rashba ferromagnet (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_96_045428_1) is a generalized two-dimensional Rashba ferromagnet used as a model system, which can include spin-independent Gaussian white-noise disorder (sources: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.085405, 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.045428, 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.161403). It exhibits antidamping-like spin-orbit torque (SOT) arising from disorder-induced interband-coherence effects, which is very sensitive to the structure of the disorder potential in the internal space (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.045428). It also exhibits intrinsic spin-orbit torque, which may have the same sign as the intrinsic SOT in the presence of spin-dependent disorder (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.045428). The material displays chiral ferromagnetism, characterized by a contribution w(ch) to the micromagnetic energy density that is linear with respect to the first spatial derivatives of the local magnetization direction (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.161403). Additionally, it shows current-induced motion of a magnetic texture with the classical drift velocity of conduction electrons (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.085405). Rashba spin-orbit coupling induces anisotropy of effective spin renormalization, Gilbert damping, and spin-transfer torques, all of which are thoroughly analyzed (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.085405). The spin susceptibility of the system is also computed (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.085405).

raw.text: Co (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_93_241401_1) is a material system that exhibits ferromagnetism across a wide range of compositions and dimensionalities. Pristine VS₂ nanosheets are ferromagnetic (10.1016/j.jallcom.2017.01.192), with monolayer VS₂ showing strong ferromagnetic ordering with a saturation magnetization (M-s) of 37 emu/cc and coercivity (H-c) of 135 Oe at 300 K (10.1002/adfm.202213295). Monolayer VSe₂ is reported as a robust room-temperature ferromagnetic semiconductor under strains from -2% to 4% (10.1007/s10853-021-06311-4), though some studies find no signatures of ferromagnetic ordering in monolayer VSe₂ (10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b01649) or report a Curie temperature of 250 K (10.1088/2053-1583/ab8b48). The VSe₂ monolayer is described as a ferromagnet with room-temperature ferromagnetism (10.1021/acsami.9b02493) and a Curie point higher than 330 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085117). Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ (CGT) is a semiconducting 2D ferromagnet with out-of-plane magnetization (10.1002/adma.201906021), exhibiting ferromagnetic order down to the monolayer (10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.153368) with a Curie temperature of 66 K in pristine form, enhanced to 240 K upon Na intercalation (10.1002/adma.202400270). CGT has T_C1 ≈ 69 K (10.1002/smll.202302240) and shows a triple point around the Curie temperature in its phase diagram (10.1103/PhysRevB.107.134417). Moderate in-plane strain can enhance ferromagnetism in Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ up to room temperature (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.L022040). CrI₃ is a prototypical van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevB.109.094415) with monolayer ferromagnetic order below 45 K (10.1088/2053-1583/aaf06d) and bulk Curie temperature of 61 K (10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b04282). Monolayer CrI₃ exhibits long-range FM order with Tc ~45 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858), while estimation yields 55-65 K (10.1088/2053-1583/ab72d8). Chlorination can increase the Curie temperature up to 204 K (10.1016/j.matchemphys.2024.129994). In bilayer CrI₃, pressure induces a transition from layered antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase (10.1038/s41563-019-0505-2), and the bilayer can be switched between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic types (10.1038/s41524-022-00706-w). Fe₃GeTe₂ (FGT) is a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1007/s12274-021-3826-9) with Curie temperatures ranging from 130-220 K (10.1002/advs.202206842), ~200 K in flakes (10.1021/acsnano.3c11480), and 220 K in bulk (10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c03111). FGT is an itinerant 2D ferromagnet (10.1021/acsnano.2c03626) with ferromagnetic states in 1-10 layer thickness (10.1038/s41699-020-00167-z) and long-range ferromagnetic order down to monolayer (10.1103/PhysRevB.100.085403). Fe₄GeTe₂ is a nearly room-temperature vdW ferromagnet (10.1103/wmb3-5r6b) with Tc = 68 K (10.1038/s42005-022-00921-3) and confirmed ferromagnetic metallic nature (10.1039/d4na00639a). Fe₅GeTe₂ is a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1021/acsnano.2c08844) with high Curie temperatures exceeding 300 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.106.045137), Tc ~315 K (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.7.044411), and a paramagnetic to ferromagnetic transition at ~302 K (10.3390/nano15010019). Cr₂Te₃ is a two-dimensional ferromagnet (10.1186/s40580-022-00348-0) with Curie temperature of 180 K (10.1080/21663831.2020.1865469) and room-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D form (10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b05128), with Tc increasing from 160 K in thick flakes to 280 K in 6 UC (7.1 nm) (10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b05128). Cr₅Te₈ exhibits robust ferromagnetic behavior with out-of-plane easy axis (10.1021/acsnano.1c11018), Curie temperature above 220 K (10.1021/acsnano.4c08700), and 176 K in nanosheets (10.1021/acsami.3c02446). CrBr₃ monolayer is a 2D ferromagnetic semiconductor with Curie temperature of 34 K (10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b00553). CrGeTe₃ is a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1007/s11433-026-2939-x) with Tc ~66 K at ambient, exceeding ~250 K under pressure (10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.217203). VI₃ is a layered van der Waals ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1103/PhysRevB.100.094402) becoming ferromagnetic at 49-50 K (10.1002/adma.201808074, 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.014105) with bulk Tc = 50 K and exfoliated multilayer Tc = 57 K (10.1021/acs.nanolett.2c01361). VTe₂ monolayer exhibits in-plane ferromagnetic ground state with Curie temperature of 377 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2020.148098). CrSiTe₃ shows ferromagnetism at high pressure (10.1021/acs.jpclett.3c00507) with finite-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.214425). Cr₂S₃ is a ferromagnetic insulator (10.1016/j.physb.2025.417396) with long-range ferromagnetic order in 2D (10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c05105). Cr₂Se₃ is ferromagnetic (10.1021/acs.chemmater.3c00172) with ferromagnetic properties below ~70 K (10.1021/acsnano.3c10609). NiCl₂ shows ferromagnetic ground state (10.7566/JPSJ.93.034710) and is a ferromagnetic insulator (10.1039/c9na00588a). FeCl₂ is a 2D ferromagnetic half-metal (10.1039/d0tc04156d). CrO₂ is half-metallic ferromagnetic (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.104428). The material exhibits ferromagnetic order maintained upon exfoliating bulk down to a few layers (10.1103/PhysRevB.98.214420) and shows coexisting ferromagnetic and ferroelectric orders in heterostructures (10.1103/PhysRevB.111.144418).

raw.name: phosphorene
raw.text: Phosphorene is a two-dimensional semiconductor with a buckled or puckered honeycomb lattice structure, composed of phosphorus atoms, and is a monolayer of black phosphorus (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/aa6fa6; 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.165122; 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.235424; 10.1103/PhysRevB.94.075106). It exhibits an indirect band gap of 1.94 eV (source: 10.1016/j.jpcs.2025.113309) and 1.93 eV via DFT (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2020.154255), and its band gap is large enough for room-temperature observation (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.241103). The material has carrier mobilities among the largest reported for a 2D material (source: 10.1021/acsami.5c07758) and can undergo electronic state transitions among metallic, half-metallic, and semiconducting states under varying strain (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2023.112668). Its bandgap is tunable with strain (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2023.112668). The plasma frequency for pristine blue phosphorene is 11.34 eV, with values of 8.6 eV for Ce-doped and 9.03 eV for Ti-doped blue phosphorene via DFT (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2020.154255). Spin-orbit coupling in phosphorene is low, reminiscent of graphene (source: 10.1021/acsami.5c07758), and the electron and hole g-factor correction is approximately 0.03 due to intrinsic contributions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.115203). The material exhibits extraordinary spin and charge transport properties (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/ad9dfd), and spin transport behavior is similar to that in a two-dimensional frustrated antiferromagnet (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2016.12.001). A highly mobile 2D hole gas (2DHG) is present near the Fermi level (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.115404). All adsorption systems have a large binding energy (source: 10.1186/s11671-018-2696-x). The main features of energy spectra create special structures in the density of states (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/aaca24). Energy-driven Coulomb drag near charge neutrality is observed due to electron-hole coupling in a broken-gap heterojunction (source: 10.1021/acsami.3c18655).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: MoSSe
raw.text: MoSSe is a thermodynamically stable nonpolar transition metal dichalcogenide alloy, specifically a monolayer Janus transition-metal dichalcogenide (MoSSe) and a 2D Janus monolayer material with out-of-plane electrical polarization, also described as a ternary transition metal dichalcogenide, a Janus MoSSe monolayer with inherent strain due to asymmetry, a Janus type of monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide, a two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide used in heterostructures, a transition metal dichalcogenides based Janus MoSSe monolayer, an asymmetric Janus structure, a Janus MoSSe monolayer with out-of-plane symmetry, a newly synthesized Janus TMDs MoSSe, a Janus monolayer material, a Janus system, a two dimensional van der Waals material component, a Janus single-layer MoSSe, a 2D Janus MoSSe, a monolayer used as a substrate for synthesizing MoCrSSe, a two-dimensional polar MoSSe, a monolayer Janus MoSSe, a Janus MoSSe monolayer, a Janus MoSSe substrate, a semiconductor used in van der Waals heterojunctions with VSe2, Janus MoSSe monolayers, and a reference two-dimensional material for comparison. It intrinsically possesses both in-plane inversion and out-of-plane mirror-symmetry breaking (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.235404), leading to strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) due to structural inversion asymmetry (source: 10.1039/d3ta03227b) and resulting in a significant Rashba effect (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c04153), with these alloys exhibiting a nonlinear anisotropic Rashba effect (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.165402). Pure single-layer MoSSe harbors an intriguing multivalleyed band structure with strong coupled spin and valley physics (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.8b01625). Asymmetric Janus structures (MoSSe, WSSe) have many exciting properties, such as out-of-plane piezoelectricity, spatial isolation of charge carriers, and strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) resulting in a significant Rashba effect (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c04153). The high binding energies for the doping of non-metal atoms into TMD sheets show energetic stability of the doped Janus sheets (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149146). A direct-to-indirect band gap transition occurs in the pristine MoSSe ML for a biaxial ([110]) compressive/tensile strain of > -/+2% (source: 10.1016/j.matchemphys.2023.128149). The maximum adsorption energy for H2S on pristine Janus MoSSe monolayer is similar to -0.156 eV, with a range of -0.156 eV to -0.238 eV (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.06.049). The maximum adsorption energy for NH3 on pristine Janus MoSSe monolayer is similar to -0.203 eV, with a range of -0.203 eV to -0.281 eV (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.06.049). The maximum adsorption energy for NO on pristine Janus MoSSe monolayer is similar to -0.117 eV (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.06.049). The maximum adsorption energy for NO2 on pristine Janus MoSSe monolayer is similar to -0.252 eV, with values of -0.252 eV (pristine), -3.360 eV (Se defect), and -3.404 eV (S/Se defect) (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.06.049). The adsorption of NO2 molecule induced about 1 mu B magnetic moment (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.06.049). A mergence of A and B excitons is predicted at a critical strength of in-plane magnetic exchange field (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.045425), and enhanced tunability of the optical absorption spectra is demonstrated via the combination of magnetic exchange fields and strain (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.045425).

raw.name: VSN
raw.text: VSN (VSi2N4) is a two-dimensional (2D) monolayer material from the MoSi2N4 family, specifically a septuple-atomic-layer layered van der Waals material with a structure of homogeneous metal nitride multilayers sandwiched between two SiN surfaces (source: 10.1007/s11467-024-1431-6, 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.064006, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.2c03963). It is a newly reported magnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.235408) and pristine VSi2N4 is a semiconductor (source: 10.1039/d3tc02817h), with semiconducting behavior confirmed across multiple studies (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.235435, 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.235408, 10.1039/d3tc02817h). It exhibits half-metallic ferromagnetic character with a high magnetic ordering temperature of 285 K (source: 10.1002/andp.202100273) and is also described as a half-metal (source: 10.1016/j.cjph.2026.01.006). VSi2N4 possesses intrinsic multiferroicity with the coexistence of out-of-plane ferroelectricity and interlayer A-type antiferromagnetism (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.085433), and is a sliding multiferroic layered material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.085433). It has a pair of Dirac-type valleys located at the corners of the hexagonal Brillouin zone (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.235435) and is a valleytronic van der Waals material (source: 10.1039/d2mh00906d) and valley-half-semiconducting material (source: 10.1038/s41524-021-00632-3). The VSi2N4/MoSi2N4 interface causes opposite bending of the conduction bands in MoSi2N4 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074002) and generates a larger and fully-spin-polarized photogalvanic effect (PGE) photocurrent (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074002). It is used as a half-metallic electrode (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074002) and as a barrier in tunneling devices (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2026.187218). When integrated with CrI3 ferromagnetic layers and Ag electrodes, it generates a giant tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) over 105% (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.104429), and the TMR and spin injection efficiency maintain high values below 0.25 V (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.104429). A spin filtering efficiency close to 100% is achieved for the VSi2N4/MoSiGeN4/VSi2N4 magnetic tunnel junction with a parallel magnetic configuration (source: 10.1016/j.cjph.2026.01.006). It exhibits a large band gap quantum spin Hall state with a hybridization gap as large as ~204 meV, realizing spin-polarized conducting edge states with nearly quantized spin Hall conductivity (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.245149). The MSN monolayer (MoSi2N4) is a semiconductor with an indirect band gap of 1.79 eV (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.150326). VSi2P4 exhibits ferromagnetic characteristics with a high Curie temperature of 350 K (source: 10.1039/d3tc03040g) and is a ferromagnetic material (source: 10.1039/d4tc03592e), also described as a type-II spin-gapless semiconductor (source: 10.1039/d3tc03040g). All molecules are physisorbed on the MSM surface with small charge transfer, acting as either charge acceptors or donors (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.150326). Layered antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal and spatial inversion symmetry exhibit lifted spin degeneracy across the entire Brillouin zone (source: 10.1103/jyq4-d4gs).
