raw.name: Bi2Se3
raw.text: Bi2Se3 is a three-dimensional layered topological insulator (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155114, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b00047, 10.1021/acsnano.2c02515, 10.1088/1367-2630/ab9201) and van der Waals topological insulator (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.113404) with an insulating bulk and gapless metallic surface states having a Dirac cone (10.1039/d4tc02226b), hosting a single surface Dirac fermion (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.115125). It exhibits spin-momentum locking (10.1021/acsami.2c08053, 10.1038/s41565-018-0195-y, 10.1021/acsnano.5c10193) and helical spin-momentum locking of the surface states arising from intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (10.1039/d4tc02226b), enabling non-local electrical detection (10.1038/s41565-018-0195-y). The material shows linear dispersion and preserved spin texture of the surface states (10.1021/acsami.2c08053), massless Dirac electrons tunnelling between helical Landau levels developed in the topological surface states at interfaces (10.1038/s41563-024-02079-5), and Rashba spin-split quantum well states (10.1038/s41535-022-00490-2). Bi2Se3 films grown on alpha-RuCl3 are heavily n-doped with n(e) ~ 10^14 cm^-2 and electron mobility mu ~ 450 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 at low temperatures from magnetotransport measurements (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.113404). High carrier mobility is also reported in solution grown ultrathin nanoplates (10.1021/acsaelm.9b00415, 10.1016/j.apsadv.2025.100867). The material exhibits weak antilocalization in Bi2Se3 and Bi2-xCoxSe3 (x <= 0.4) (10.1063/5.0011134), anomalous magnetotransport with giant negative magnetoresistance at the Dirac point up to about -91% (10.1021/acsnano.7b02494), and acoustic phonon modes at 24.04 ± 2.05 GHz and 48.11 ± 2.02 GHz induced by ultrafast laser pulses (10.1016/j.cjph.2024.08.030). Bi2Se3 thin films exhibit highly c-axis preferred orientation and six-fold symmetric diffraction patterns of Bi2Se3{015} facets (10.1016/j.cjph.2024.08.030), and atomically smooth and uniform surfaces when grown by molecular beam epitaxy (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.113404). The material shows chemical diffusion where Se outdiffuses from Bi2Se3 into a growing Mn film (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.054001), and twin planes repel each other at least over a vertical distance of 3-4 nm (10.3390/nano10102059). Volume doping preserves non-trivial topology in Bi1.98Fe0.02Se3 (10.1088/1367-2630/ab890d). The material exhibits emergence of topological Chern bands with Chern numbers C = +/- 1 (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.115125) and an unconventional band-gap response with a large Chern number C = +/- 3 (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155114). Bi2Se3 is used as a base material for dilute ferromagnetic topological insulators (10.1002/adma.202209951), in heterostructures with CrSBr (10.1038/s41524-022-00802-x), and as a Bi2Se3 nanoplate stacked with monolayer graphene to form a vertical heterojunction (10.1021/acsnano.6b00659).

raw.text: Bi2Te3 is a three-dimensional layered topological insulator (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155114, 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.5.L022019, 10.1039/d5na00136f) and an archetypical topological insulator (10.1103/PhysRevB.100.121104) that hosts a single surface Dirac fermion (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.115125) with spin-momentum-locked topological surface states (10.1021/acsnano.5c17764) and topologically protected surface states insensitive to nonmagnetic disorder (10.1103/PhysRevB.108.035408). It is a non-magnetic quintuple layer (QL) material (10.1088/2053-1583/ac3cc6) and a centrosymmetric material used as a quintuple layer in heterostructures (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.5.013001), with a van der Waals nature of interlayer forces (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.7.034201) and a van der Waals gap (10.1016/j.jallcom.2020.156153). The material exhibits highly c-axis orientation (textured films) (10.1016/j.jallcom.2016.09.109) and two Raman-active modes: E-g(2) at 102.5 cm(-1) and A(1g)(2) at 134.8 cm(-1) as measured by Raman spectroscopy (10.1016/j.jallcom.2016.09.109). Electrical doping is achieved via reaction with iron salts (FeCl2) (10.1063/5.0220681), and this doping method preserves the bulk-insulating properties of the topological insulator (10.1021/acsnano.5c17764). In Bi2Te3/TiOx/NZFO samples, the thinnest TiOx barriers result in an antiferromagnetic (AFM) disordered interfacial layer due to diffusion, while increasing TiOx barrier thickness reduces diffusion but maintains strong interfacial magnetic exchange-interaction and a large spin-pumping effect from the magnetic material across the TiOx to the topological insulator surface states (10.1002/admi.202201691). The magnetic proximity effect from MnBi2Te4 septuple layers yields finite and tunable shift and injection photocurrents in Bi2Te3 under linearly polarized light irradiation, with magnetic injection photoconductivity localized on the Bi2Te3 layer reaching >70 x 10^8 A/(V^2 s), and pure photogenerated spin current is also observed (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.5.013001). The material exhibits emergence of topological Chern bands on the surface with Chern numbers C = +/- 1 (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.115125), and an unconventional band-gap response to the magnetic exchange field is accompanied by a large Chern number C = +/- 3 (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155114). The conductor supporting the voltage signal is the topologically protected two-dimensional surface-state system at the interface between a ferromagnetic insulator and a topological insulator (10.1103/PhysRevB.95.165418). Bi2Te3 serves as a reference material for comparison with MnBi2Te4 (10.1103/7kzb-41xm), a degradation product of MnBi2Te4 (10.1088/0256-307X/43/5/050713), a competing binary phase in the synthesis reaction of MnBi2Te4 (10.1038/s41524-020-00427-y), and a component of the MnTe-Bi2Te3 system as a prototype structure for the homologous series (10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.03.030). It is a component of the MnBi2Te4/(Bi2Te3)n family (10.1021/acs.jpclett.3c00162), including (MnBi2Te4)(Bi2Te3)(m) films (10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c01817) and MnBi4Te7 natural superlattices (10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.107204), as well as a component of natural van der Waals superlattices (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.014203) and superlattice-like layered structures in the Mn-Bi-Te family (10.1088/0256-307X/42/9/090702). It is also a component of the MnTe-SnTe-Bi2Te3 pseudo-ternary system (10.1016/j.matchemphys.2026.132365). The material is used as a topological insulator spacer layer in heterostructures (10.1021/acsami.4c19932, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.1c01874), a separation layer in MnBi2Te4(Bi2Te3)n compounds (10.1103/PhysRevB.100.155144), a capping layer (10.1039/d2nr04820e), a substrate (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.7.054005, 10.1002/smll.202504498), and a van der Waals heterostructure component (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.064431). It is described as a two-dimensional (2D) single-crystal bismuth telluride plate (10.1063/5.0220681), a layered material (10.1016/j.mtchem.2023.101646), and a semi-magnetic topological insulator when doped with Mn atoms in substitutional (Mn-Bi) and interstitial van der Waals gap positions (Mn-i) (10.1103/PhysRevB.93.214409). The coupling between ferromagnetic and topological characteristics is noted (10.1002/adom.202500951).

raw.name: C2N
raw.text: C2N (also referred to as C3N, C₃N, or 2D polyaniline) is a two-dimensional (2D) material with a graphene-like honeycomb structure, described as a carbon layered honeycomb-like compound with a 3D network structure formerly studied and devised here in a 2D layered AIB(2)-type derived structure, a nitrogen-graphene crystal, a 2D crystalline, hole-free extension of graphene, a recently synthesized graphene-like carbon nitride monolayer, a holey 2D C2N monolayer, a 2D material with large pores, a two-dimensional material with pores used as a host for single-atom catalysts, a carbon-nitride component of van der Waals heterostructures, a two-dimensional carbon nitride material, an atomically thin carbon nitride sheet, a two-dimensional (2D) carbon nitride, a two-dimensional (2D) organic metal-free material, a wide bandgap semiconductor 2D material, a newly discovered two-dimensional quantum material, a two-dimensional monolayer material, and graphene-like nanoribbons (zigzag C3N nanoribbons, ZC(3)NNRs). Pristine C2N is a semiconductor (source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2017.02.069). C₃N is an indirect-band semiconductor with an energy gap of 0.38 eV (source: 10.1007/s11467-017-0741-3); C3N is a semiconductor with an indirect bandgap of 0.39 eV (source: 10.1002/adma.201605625); the C3N monolayer is a semiconductor with a band gap of 0.36 eV (method: tight-binding model; source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417209); the C3N monolayer has semiconductor properties with an indirect band gap of 1.128 eV (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2024.113652); the presence of the intrinsic band gap of 3.06 eV makes atomically thin carbon nitride sheets (CNs) a promising spin-based semiconductor material (source: 10.1021/acsnano.1c03396); the band gap decreases with increasing layer thickness (source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2019.10.038). The work function of C2N can be effectively modulated by metal doping from 5.25 eV for pristine C2N (source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2017.02.069). It exhibits ferromagnetic narrow gap semiconductor properties with a Curie temperature of 204 K (method: Monte Carlo simulation; source: 10.1016/j.physb.2018.11.003) and has stable electron spin polarization with a magnetic moment of each primitive cell of 1 μB (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2018.11.003). Corner states can be fully spin polarized and moved into the bulk states via magnetic exchange field (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L161110). van Hove singularities are located at energies near the Fermi level, which is half that of graphene (source: 10.1007/s11467-017-0741-3). Materials possess flat bands near their Fermi level (31 materials; source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2024.119277). Materials display characteristics of normal metals (664 materials; source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2024.119277), semiconductors (664 materials; source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2024.119277), and semimetal behavior (57 materials; source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2024.119277). Electrical conductivity calculations reveal intriguing properties for the C3N monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417209). The electric conductivity of C2N is significantly influenced by CO, NO, HCN, CS2, and SO2 molecules (source: 10.1016/j.jpcs.2023.111720). Electronic heat capacity increases with increasing tensile biaxial strain and reduces with compressive biaxial strain (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2025.417209). Introduction of defect significantly enhances its conductivity (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2024.113652). NO adsorption of pristine C2N and Fe2@C2N monolayers exhibited half-metallicity behavior and magnetic properties (source: 10.1016/j.jpcs.2023.111720).

raw.text: TiS₂ is a 2D layered chalcogenide compound based on Ti and S (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.044002), classified as a Group IV transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.cjph.2020.03.018) and a van der Waals material (source: 10.1016/j.matdes.2025.114176). It is a parent titanium dichalcogenide compound (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ae30fb) and a layered compound host for iron intercalation (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.7.014401), also described as layered TiS₂ sulphides (source: 10.1039/d2tc02160a) and a layered compound (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2024.177905). Structurally, it exists as XS₂ with X = Ti in the monolayer MoS₂ structure with trigonal-prismatic coordination (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.035120) and as a 3d transition metal dichalcogenide with octahedral 1T and trigonal prismatic 2H structures (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.115115). In its pristine form, TiS₂ is a non-magnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ae30fb; 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416413), with the ideal crystal symmetry of the 1T-TiS₂ lattice resulting in a non-magnetic structure (source: 10.3390/nano15181435); specifically, pristine monolayer TiS₂ is a non-magnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416413), while pristine 1T-TiS₂ is weakly semiconducting (source: 10.3390/nano15181435). The bands near the Fermi energy primarily exhibit d orbital characters, well separated from other bands with p character, indicating semiconducting behavior (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416413). Upon substituting 3d-TM atoms, a variety of electronic and magnetic phases emerge, including magnetic half-metal and magnetic metal (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2024.416413). Structural stability of 2D layered chalcogenides was investigated, with most stable phases determined for each compound (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.044002).

raw.name: Ca(CoN)2
raw.text: Ca(CoN)2 is a monolayer transition metal nitride (source: 10.1002/adfm.202505282) and a two-dimensional altermagnet (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01776-2), specifically described as a special twisted altermagnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.L220402) and a representative example of a two-dimensional monolayer altermagnet (source: 10.1103/643d-wkc1) with valley-mediated spin-layer coupling (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.056401); it is also reported as a bilayer altermagnetic material protected by S4z symmetry (source: 10.1103/9jmx-fg25). The material exhibits an anomalous Hall effect, where sliding along the x or y axis induces layer-locked Berry curvature and spin-valley-layer polarized AHE (source: 10.1103/9jmx-fg25). It shows layer-dependent spin Hall conductivity, which remains symmetry-permitted and exhibits distinct layer-dependent behavior (source: 10.1103/643d-wkc1). Additionally, it has a vanishing anomalous Hall conductivity due to symmetry-enforced spin-layer coupling configurations that lead to cancellation of oppositely signed layer-resolved contributions (source: 10.1103/643d-wkc1), and it is characterized by alternating spin-split bands and zero net magnetization (source: 10.1103/643d-wkc1).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: 2D ferromagnets
raw.text: 2D ferromagnets (mat_10_1021_acs_jpclett_9b01969_1) are two-dimensional ferroics including ferromagnets (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b01969), with numerous ferromagnetic materials found in databases for two-dimensional materials (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-0300-2), and a class of two-dimensional ferromagnetic materials searched via high-throughput computation (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00813-8). They exhibit ferromagnetism (sources: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b01969, 10.1038/s41524-020-0300-2), with Curie temperature properties including the discovery of 26 materials with a Curie point beyond 400 K (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-0300-2) and Co₂F₂ having the highest T-C = 541 K, well above room temperature, as determined by first-principles computation (source: 10.1038/s41524-022-00813-8). In two-dimensional magnets with ferromagnetic Heisenberg interaction and in-plane DM interaction (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.214421), the thermal Hall effect can be induced when an out-of-plane magnetic field is applied and persists even when the magnetic field is large (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.214421). Spin fluctuations in two-dimensional ferromagnets in the presence of crystalline lattice dislocations are investigated (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.165146), revealing that bulk topology existing in the perfect crystal is robust under the influence of lattice defects (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.165146), and that the topology of magnonic dislocation modes remains unaffected when bulk topology becomes trivial and is remarkably resilient against magnetic disorder (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.165146). Additionally, the existence of topologically protected nonpropagative modes that localize at dislocations is shown (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.165146). Canonical two-dimensional ferromagnets are used for comparison (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/42/11/110713).

raw.text: 2D multiferroics, also referred to as two-dimensional magnetoelectric multiferroics, exhibit coupled ferroic orders (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b01969). raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: Yttrium Iron Garnet
raw.text: Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG, Y₃Fe₅O₁₂) is a widely used magnetic material, specifically a ferrimagnetic insulator, ferromagnetic insulator, and above-room-temperature ferrimagnet, often employed as a thin film nanostructure, single-crystalline thin film, magnetic substrate, or in heterostructures such as Pt/YIG bilayers (10.1002/adfm.201805592, 10.1103/PhysRevB.95.165418, WOS:001334812700001, 10.1088/1367-2630/abfd00, 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L121403, 10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.156703, 10.1021/acsnano.7b05743, 10.1038/s41563-022-01369-0, 10.1063/1.5001318, 10.1063/5.0306423, 10.1103/PhysRevB.99.214446, 10.1039/d4tc04702h, 10.1039/d3nh00137g, 10.1039/d5ta03991f, 10.1088/1367-2630/ad26b9, 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.014408, 10.1002/adfm.202003192, 10.1088/2053-1583/4/1/014001, 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.174440, 10.1021/acsnano.5c10540, 10.1088/2053-1583/aa6663, 10.1007/s12274-023-5865-x, 10.1021/acsnano.1c07192, 10.1063/5.0189993, 10.1039/d3ta01702h, 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.064202, 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.184409, 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.241405, 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.060402, 10.1021/acsami.0c22345, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c03499). It exhibits low damping, high Curie temperature, and high resistivity (10.1002/adfm.201805592), and hosts long-lived magnons (10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L121403). It enables efficient spin-to-charge conversions (SCCs) via either the inverse spin Hall effect or the inverse Rashba-Edelstein effect (IREE) in graphene by proximity with an adjacent spin-orbit coupling (SOC) material, as demonstrated in single-layer graphene integrated with YIG and Py (10.1088/2053-1583/ac3c9b, 10.1103/PhysRevB.99.214446). The spin current density and effective spin mixing conductance, measured by ferromagnetic resonance, are among the highest reported in the literature (10.1039/d3nh00137g). The exchange coupling strength is determined to be as high as 27 meV (10.1063/1.5001318). A two-dimensional magnon spin conductivity around 1 S at room temperature is extracted (10.1038/s41563-022-01369-0). It enables imaging with multiple localized standing spin-wave modes confined by the micromagnetic tip (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.184409). It exhibits a parametric magnon-phonon coupling m dagger m(b dagger+b) (10.1088/1367-2630/ad26b9). The spin-Seebeck effect refers to voltage signals induced in metals by thermally driven spin currents in adjacent magnetic systems (10.1103/PhysRevB.95.165418). Surface spin wave supplements an additional freedom of surface plasmon excitation (10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.156703, WOS:001334812700001). It is a benchmark magnetic material for quantum magnonics (10.1063/5.0306423) and a reference material for comparison of magnon conductivity (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.174440).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: Nb3Cl8
raw.text: Nb3Cl8 is a two-dimensional breathing kagome van der Waals material, described as a kagome semiconductor, a cluster Mott insulator, a breathing kagome lattice van der Waals material, a two-dimensional breathing-Kagome magnet, a 2D intrinsic multiferroic semiconductor with a breathing kagome lattice, a two-dimensional multiferroic semiconductor with a breathing Kagome lattice, a two-dimensional multiferroic breathing kagome material, a displacement-type antiferroelectric bilayer material, a layered antiferromagnet with broken time-reversal and spatial inversion symmetry, a two-dimensional van der Waals material, a van der Waals layered compound, a breathing-mode kagome van der Waals material, an emerging topological semiconducting material with a van der Waals layered structure, a two-dimensional crystalline material with Kagome structure, a triangular lattice Mott insulator, a layered Mott-Hubbard insulator, a magnetic insulator/barrier material with intrinsic electric polarization in van der Waals junctions, an emergent van der Waals (vdW) magnetic semiconductor, a component of the breathing kagome Nb3X8 family, an obstructed atomic insulator (OAI), a van der Waals semiconductor with a breathing kagome lattice, an insulating van der Waals material used as a ferroelectric layer, a two-dimensional material with stacking-dependent magnetic properties, a breathing kagome semiconductor, a van der Waals nanofilm, a conventional material with flat-band correlations and valley properties, a stable layered bulk phase, a breathing Kagome lattice-based material, and a 2D ferromagnetic monolayer. It exhibits ferroelectricity with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization directions corresponding to the breathing process of kagome lattice trimer patterns and broken spatial inversion symmetry; the ferroelectric transition controls the local sublattice symmetry in the ferroelectric monolayer (sources: 10.1039/d3tc00560g, 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.115407, 10.1103/rrs6-83v6). It shows pronounced optical anisotropy, with a refractive index of 4.5 in-plane vs 2.75 out-of-plane, optical conductivity of 8000 (Ω·cm)⁻¹ in-plane vs 100 (Ω·cm)⁻¹ out-of-plane, and absorption coefficient of 10⁵ cm⁻¹ in-plane vs 10⁴ cm⁻¹ out-of-plane (source: 10.1016/j.mssp.2024.108238). It is a semiconductor with a narrow bandgap energy of 1.23 eV (source: 10.1016/j.mssp.2024.108238) and a moderate band gap due to the absence of inversion symmetry (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.2c00778). Metallization occurs at 25.4 GPa under nonhydrostatic conditions and is delayed by ~2.0 GPa under hydrostatic conditions (source: 10.1103/k3fv-9hss). It exhibits an in-plane 120° cycloid of trimerized spins as the ground state (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/add026). The Nb₃X₈ (X = Cl, Br, I) monolayers possess biocompatible properties (source: 10.1039/c6nr07231c). It is ferromagnetic with a Curie temperature Tc = 31 K for Nb₃Cl₈ (method: mean field approximation based on classical Heisenberg model; source: 10.1039/c6nr07231c). ARPES results depict the presence of multiple flat and weakly dispersing bands (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L121404), with spectroscopic evidence of flat and weakly dispersing bands in breathing-kagome semiconductor Nb₃I₈ around 500 meV binding energy (source: 10.1038/s43246-022-00318-3). It exhibits strong infrared light absorption (source: 10.1039/c6nr07231c). The FE-AFMs exhibit lifted spin degeneracy across the entire Brillouin zone (source: 10.1103/jyq4-d4gs). A linear magnetoelectric response is proposed but forbidden by the presence of helical order (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/add026). For Nb₃Br₈ and Nb₃I₈, long period incommensurate helical order is found (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/add026).

raw.name: InS
raw.text: InS is a group-IIIA metal-monochalcogenide monolayer (source: 10.1088/2053-1583/4/1/015017), also described as a honeycomb InS monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.155240) and a group III monochalcogenide monolayer (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c03994). It is a two-dimensional material used as a tunnel barrier (source: 10.1039/d3nr04712a), a 2D van der Waals multiferroic material component (source: 10.1002/adfm.202504772), and a two-dimensional ferroelectric material (source: 10.1016/j.cjph.2025.01.015). It is also identified as a ferroelectric In2S3 monolayer (source: 10.1021/acssensors.2c02365) and a ferroelectric substrate selected for FeClI (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.085401), used as a ferroelectric layer in a heterobilayer (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.205307) and as a component of the AgCr2Te4/In2S3 heterobilayer (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c05775). InS is used to form a heterostructure with Sc2COHH (source: 10.1039/d1ta00614b). The bandgap of pristine InS reaches a maximum at the application of -6% strain (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.155240). It exhibits reversible switching capability of ferroelectric polarization when reversing the ferroelectric polarization of the substrate In2S3 (source: 10.1016/j.cjph.2025.01.015). Under light illumination, InS can trigger homogeneous magnetism, showing strong ferromagnetic ordering induced by majority carriers (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c03994).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: InSe
raw.text: InSe (indium selenide) is a two-dimensional (2D) layered chalcogenide semiconductor and a group III monochalcogenide van der Waals material, often studied as a monolayer (e.g., pristine InSe monolayer is an indirect gap semiconductor with a band gap of 1.41 eV, source: 10.1039/d4na01013b). It exhibits high electron mobility (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.115304) and large Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in field-effect transistors (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.045307), with SOC strength for electrons near the conduction band edge in few-layer gamma-InSe films tunable over a wide range depending on film thickness and electric field (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.125432). The g factor for InSe was extracted from polarized emission and Kerr measurements (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.115304). A negative magnetoresistance of 40% at 2K under 9T magnetic field is observed (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/37/8/087401). Electrons transferred from adsorbed TM atoms to the support achieve an n-doping effect in the InSe monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2018.03.067). Under light illumination, photoinduced ferromagnetism can trigger strong ferromagnetic ordering induced by majority carriers in a group III monochalcogenide monolayer (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c03994). InSe is also a ferroelectric material, specifically alpha-In2Se3, which is a two-dimensional ferroelectric (sources: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c03452, 10.1039/d1mh00939g) exhibiting ferroelectric polarization (sources: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.2c00564, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c03970) with opposite polarization states associated with different topological phases (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00305-9). The system is trivial, while it becomes a QSHI with a sizable band gap upon polarization reversal (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00305-9). Ferroelectric monolayers are reported (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.L060406), and the heterostructure includes an In2Se3 ferroelectric monolayer (source: 10.1039/d1nr01093j). Coexistence of ferroelectricity, magnetism and topological order occurs in a two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructure composed of ferroelectric alpha-In2Se3 (source: 10.1039/d3tc04392d). The material exhibits nonvolatile ferroelectric polarization with upward or downward orientation (source: 10.1039/d1nr06383a) and an intrinsic polarisation state that can significantly modulate its electronic properties (source: 10.1039/d1nr06906c). Ferroelectric bistability can be recovered when the alpha-In2Se3 layer is thicker than three unit cells (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.235445). The ferroelectric barrier has a low energy barrier for switching (source: 10.1007/s40843-024-3291-3). Pure In2Se3 is diamagnetic (source: 10.1007/s40843-019-1212-x). Maximum electroresistance values predicted for the AMFTJ device are 2.41 x 10^5% in equilibrium state and 4.97 x 10^5% under external bias voltage (method: first-principles calculation; source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.045404). The device achieves an RA product below 1 ohm μm² (method: first-principles calculations; source: 10.1007/s40843-024-3291-3). The ON-state current density is enhanced to 10^4 A cm-2 (source: 10.1038/s41565-025-02065-1). The strength of Rashba spin splitting in the GaTe/alpha-In2Se3 heterobilayer has been significantly enhanced several times with respect to the intrinsic alpha-In2Se3 monolayer (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.085110). Total polarization of the heterostructures can be precisely modulated through reversible polarization switching in In2Se3 (source: 10.1021/acsanm.5c02573).

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: magnetic van der Waals bilayers
raw.text: Magnetic van der Waals bilayers are low-dimensional materials consisting of two layers held by van der Waals forces, composed of two monolayers (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.024506, 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.104422), and are untwisted bilayer van der Waals materials (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.115102). These systems exhibit an interlayer Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, which is nonzero due to changes in lattice symmetry (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.115102). They also display a mesoscopic FFLO state, where the proximity effect at superconductor/ferromagnet interfaces produces damped oscillatory behavior of the Cooper-pair wave function within the ferromagnetic regions, analogous to inhomogeneous Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.024506). Additionally, they host electric skyrmions, which are topological solitons formed by local dipoles requiring harsher conditions for stability; magnetic skyrmions, which are topological solitons in real space with spin moments; and ME skyrmions, emerging quasiparticles resulting from the imprint of magnetic skyrmions onto electric degrees of freedom (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.104422). A specific feature of the proximity effect in these vdW bilayer systems is the presence of nonlocal Cooper pairs (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.024506).

raw.text: CoOx (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_101_014447_2) is an antiferromagnetic layer formed by naturally oxidizing the Co surface (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.014447), and the unpressurized sample exhibited antiferromagnetic Co3O4 nanoparticles (source: 10.1016/j.carbon.2024.119437). The antiferromagnetic CoOx layer modulates the exchange bias field and coercivity by gate voltage application through a dielectric layer, clearly observed below the blocking temperature T-B (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.014447). Cobalt and iron oxides, due to their tunable structural and magnetic properties, are widely studied for electronic and spintronic applications (source: 10.1039/d5tc01923k). CoOx also serves as a precursor oxide layer in the superlattice (source: 10.1002/advs.202201749), as a component of the CoCl2/Co3O4 heterojunction and base material for comparison (source: 10.1002/smll.202305641), and as nanopillars embedded in the Bi2WO6 matrix (source: 10.1007/s12274-021-3429-5).

raw.name: CoCl2
raw.text: CoCl2 is a two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dihalide (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.054305), also described as a 2D metal dihalide with M = Co and X = Cl (source: 10.1021/acsnano.4c04397), a transition metal dihalide with M=Co, X=Cl (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.044001), a 2D transition metal dichloride (source: 10.1039/c8tc00443a), a binary transition metal dihalide precursor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084003), a buckled monolayer 2D transition metal halide (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1), a two-dimensional AB2 bilayer candidate material (source: 10.1103/twhq-32db), a two-dimensional magnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01949-z), a two-dimensional ferromagnetic semiconductor (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.L201403), a component of the CoCl2/Co3O4 heterojunction (source: 10.1002/smll.202305641), and a 2D auxetic magnet protected by P4 over bar m2 crystal symmetry (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.134438). Transition-metal dihalides (TMDH) are emerging as a highly promising class of 2D magnetic materials (source: 10.1021/acsnano.5c02175). CoCl2 exhibits remarkable in-plane auxetic behavior with a negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) (source: 10.1038/s41524-020-00424-1) and also exhibits a negative Poisson ratio, expanding laterally when stretched (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.134438). It hosts weakly dispersive flat bands arising from localized d orbitals (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01949-z). Notable in-plane spin canting is observed when polaron II is formed (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.054305). The 2D transition metal dihalide is an ideal platform for small polaron formation, with three distinct structures of small polarons identified: charges localized on one, two, and three Co atoms (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.054305). The photoexcited charge carrier lifetime for the spin-minority channel is distinctly reduced by the spin-polarized polaron state in the band gap, making it four orders of magnitude shorter than the spin-majority channel (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.054305). Due to large Coulomb interaction, U/W > 1 (with the bandwidth W) in most TM halides, making them strongly correlated materials (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.034001). Various types of chiral antiferromagnetic spin configurations can be achieved (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.134438).

raw.name: GdI2
raw.text: GdI2 is a layered van der Waals bulk material (10.1039/d0mh00183j) from which monolayer GdI2 can be exfoliated (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.125121), classified as a two-dimensional material (10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c00597), a 2D van der Waals magnet (10.1039/d2nr01757a), a 2D van der Waals material (10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c01948), a two-dimensional magnet (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.054424), a rare-earth halide (10.1088/2053-1583/ad7b52), a ferromagnetic electride (10.1016/j.surfin.2024.104597), a 2D Gd halide material (10.1021/acsaelm.2c00384), a rare-earth monolayer GdX2 (X = Cl, Br, I) (10.1016/j.mtphys.2021.100514), and a two-dimensional rare-earth metal halide (10.1140/epjp/s13360-023-04207-7). It is a component of the GdI2/GeC van der Waals heterostructure (10.1016/j.jallcom.2023.170848) and is investigated for spin-valley physics (10.1103/6wl8-r9zw). Monolayer GdCl2, a related material, is a FM semiconductor with strong FM coupling (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428), a hexagonal structure (10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L081116), and is proposed as a potential candidate material for valleytronic applications (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428); it exhibits perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with the easy axis along the out-of-plane direction (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428), piezoelectricity with the only independent piezoelectric strain coefficient d(11) = -2.708 pm/V (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428), semiconducting behavior as a FM semiconductor (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428), and spontaneous valley polarization with a valley splitting of 42.3 meV due to its intrinsic ferromagnetism and spin-orbit coupling (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428). The Eu-substituted monolayer remains a ferromagnetic semiconductor with a large 4f magnetic moment just like the parent monolayer (10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L081116). Monolayer GdF2 is predicted to be a ferrovalley material with dynamic and mechanical stabilities (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428), exhibiting piezoelectricity with d(11) = 0.584 pm/V and valley splitting of 47.6 meV (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.224428). Robust ferromagnetism with large exchanges comes from the 4f(7) + 5d(1) hybridization of Gd2+ (10.1021/acsaelm.2c00384). The recently predicted ferromagnetic GdBr2 single-layer is also noted (10.1016/j.jpcs.2025.113294).

raw.name: Sb2Te3
raw.text: Sb₂Te₃ is a tetradymite-type, nonmagnetic van der Waals layered material synthesized via a solid-state method, described as a topological insulator (including three-dimensional, thin-film, and vdW topological insulator variants), a topological material, a nonmagnetic two-dimensional system with sizable spin-orbital coupling, a layered material with properties of both a topological insulator and a phase-change material, a substrate material, a base material for magnetic defects forming AFM dimer singlets, a topological insulator host material for V-doped variant, and a component of the (MnSb₂Te₄)•(Sb₂Te₃)n family and superlattice structures. It possesses topological surface states (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2019.08.009) and exhibits a Moiré topological surface state characterized by scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03535). The material shows helical Landau levels developed in the topological surface states at the interfaces, with energy-momentum-spin resonance of massless Dirac electrons tunnelling between these levels (source: 10.1038/s41563-024-02079-5). A layer Hall effect is observed, where the Hall response arises from the opposite deflection of electrons on top and bottom layers (source: 10.1103/tdx6-gnxz). Topological insulators like Sb₂Te₃ are known for their high spin-charge interconversion efficiency (source: 10.1002/adfm.202303878). In electrochemical testing (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2021.159378), Sb₂Te₃ exhibits high initial capacities of 588 mAh/g for Li cells, 521 mAh/g for Na cells, and 906 mAh/g for K cells. Direct evidence of alloying and intercalation reactions is observed in the Li system, while alloying is inferred for the K and Na systems, and conversion reactions occur for all systems. However, capacity fade is rapid in all cases, with second discharge capacities dropping to 396 mAh/g for Li, 173 mAh/g for Na, and 98 mAh/g for K half cells, and tenth cycle discharge capacities decreasing to 195 mAh/g for Li, 26 mAh/g for Na, and 24 mAh/g for K half cells. Additionally, Sb₂Te₃ has a high resistivity between 0.072 and 2.03 Ω·cm at 300 K, increasing with cooling (source: 10.1021/acsaelm.2c00966).

raw.name: La2O3Mn2Se2
raw.text: La2O3Mn2Se2 is a correlated insulating layered d-wave altermagnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.9.024402) and a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic candidate with a Lieb lattice geometry (source: 10.1103/q863-3sfx), also described as a layered altermagnet material (source: 10.1038/s43246-025-00966-1). It exhibits altermagnetism as a magnetically ordered tetragonal oxychalcogenide with dx2-y2-wave-like spin-momentum locking (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.9.024402). Magnetic measurements confirm an antiferromagnetic transition below T_N ≈ 166 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.9.024402), and neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals 2D short-range magnetic order persisting above the Néel temperature (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.9.024402). Inelastic neutron scattering yields a first-neighbor exchange interaction of J1 = 2.34(3) meV and two distinct second-neighbor altermagnetic exchange interactions of J2 = 0.56(2) meV and J2' = 0.41(4) meV, establishing the material as a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet (source: 10.1103/q863-3sfx). This demonstration of a d-wave altermagnet that allows magnon spin currents underscores the promise of altermagnets for magnonics (source: 10.1103/q863-3sfx). Under pressure, La2O3Mn2Se2 undergoes a unique pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transition (source: 10.1038/s43246-025-00966-1), accompanied by an unusual in-plane lattice collapse instead of conventional out-of-plane collapse (source: 10.1038/s43246-025-00966-1). The pressure-driven Mott phase transition exhibits orbital-selective characteristics (source: 10.1038/s43246-025-00966-1), involving a spin-state transition of Mn2+ from a high-spin (HS, S = 5/2) state to an intermediate-spin (IS, S = 3/2) state (source: 10.1038/s43246-025-00966-1).

content.text: layered triangular lattice material crystallizing in the trigonal space group R-3m

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: K2Co(SeO3)2
raw.text: K2Co(SeO3)2 is a layered triangular lattice material crystallizing in the trigonal space group R-3m (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406). The magnetic Co2+ ions form a spin-1/2 triangular lattice and display strongly frustrated magnetism, with in-plane inverse susceptibility typical of frustrated magnets and no evidence for in-plane ordering (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406). Field-and direction-dependent magnetization measurements at 2 K indicate that the material has a magnetic easy axis perpendicular to the triangular planes (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406). At around 10 K, a ferromagnetic component appears in the magnetic susceptibility perpendicular to the triangular planes (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406). The magnetic properties are sensitive to the field applied perpendicular to the triangular planes, which induces a metamagnetization transition at 0.75 T (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406). Spin polarization develops along with the increasing out-of-plane field, resulting in a saturated ferromagnetic state at high out-of-plane fields (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.4.084406).

raw.name: LaBr2
raw.text: LaBr2 is a material system (mat_10_1021_acsami_8b14037_4) that exhibits ferromagnetism. Evidence from multiple sources describes ferromagnetic properties in various related materials, including pristine VS2 nanosheets (10.1016/j.jallcom.2017.01.192), 1T-VS2 monolayer and CrAs monolayer for realizing ferromagnetic SOTIs (10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c03109), monolayer VS2 with strong ferromagnetic ordering (saturation magnetization M-s of 37 emu/cc, coercivity H-c of 135 Oe at 300 K) (10.1002/adfm.202213295), VSe2 monolayer as a room-temperature ferromagnetic semiconductor under strain (-2% to 4%) (10.1007/s10853-021-06311-4), and a phase without a ferromagnetic ground state (10.1103/PhysRevB.104.125430). The Curie temperature from electrical transport is approximately 40 K (10.1002/aelm.202101383), while VSe2 monolayer exhibits room-temperature ferromagnetism (10.1021/acsami.9b02493). Monolayer VS2 and VSe2 are ferromagnetic (10.1088/1367-2630/18/11/113038), with VSe2 monolayer reported as ferromagnetic with Curie point >330 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085117) and strong ferromagnetic ordering (10.1038/s41565-018-0063-9). Some reports indicate monolayer ferromagnetism with T-c above room temperature (10.1007/s12274-022-4400-9), while others find no ferromagnetic ordering in monolayer VSe₂ (10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b01649) or an ordering temperature of 250 K (10.1088/2053-1583/ab8b48). Monolayers of VSe2 are predicted ferromagnetic (10.1103/PhysRevB.96.235147). CrI3 monolayer remains FM with T-C ~75K (10.1209/0295-5075/114/47001). Strong ferromagnetism enhancement is seen in Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ (10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c00201). The material is described as a ferromagnetic two-dimensional (2D) material (10.1103/PhysRevB.106.085116) with coexisting ferromagnetic and ferroelectric orders in heterostructures (10.1103/PhysRevB.111.144418). In Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ (CGT), in-plane and out-of-plane resonance fields merge at Curie Temperature (TC) (10.1016/j.jallcom.2022.167401), and ferromagnetic order is maintained upon exfoliation (10.1103/PhysRevB.98.214420). Ferromagnetic van der Waals (vdW) crystals are recognized as multicaloric materials (10.1016/j.apmt.2025.102749). Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ is a semiconducting 2D ferromagnet with out-of-plane magnetization (10.1002/adma.201906021), pristine TC of 66 K, enhanced to 240 K by Na intercalation (10.1002/adma.202400270), and air exposure yields secondary ferromagnetic Cr₂Te₃ with T_C2 ≈ 160 K (10.1002/smll.202302240). It is a 2D ferromagnetic Cr2Ge2Te6 crystal (10.1002/advs.202103229) with ferromagnetic order in layers (10.1038/s41699-022-00315-7), a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.013139), and a ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1002/adfm.202214203). Two-dimensional ferromagnetic Cr2Ge2Te6 (10.1021/acsami.7b14795) acts as a ferromagnetic tunnel barrier with anisotropic magnetic moments (10.1002/adma.202314190). Critical properties of single-crystalline semiconducting ferromagnet Cr2Ge2Te6 were investigated (10.1103/PhysRevB.96.054406), with thickness-dependent paramagnetic to ferromagnetic phase transformation (10.1103/PhysRevB.109.165405). Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ is a 2D ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.196402) with accurate magnetic orientation detection (10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c02965), a ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1002/adfm.202526564), a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1039/d0nr06054b), and a rare layered ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1016/j.physb.2020.412344). The two-dimensional ferromagnet Cr2Ge2Te6 (CGT) (10.1038/s41535-022-00435-9) is well-established (10.1016/j.commatsci.2024.113542), with phase diagrams disclosing a triple point around Curie temperature (10.1103/PhysRevB.107.134417). Cr2Ge2Te6 has a Curie temperature matching AHE hysteresis loops persisting to ~60 K (10.1021/acs.nanolett.8b05121), retains long-range ferromagnetic order in monolayer form (10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.153368), is a naturally stable two-dimensional ferromagnetic material (10.3389/fphy.2023.1188513), a quasi-two-dimensional ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevB.99.165109), with intrinsic ferromagnetism (10.1039/c9nr03752g), and one of few naturally forming ferromagnetic semiconductors (10.1088/2053-1583/3/2/025035). Quasi-two-dimensional ferromagnets like Cr-2(Ge,Si)(2)Te-6 show peculiar magnetization temperature dependence (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.014440). The material shows ferromagnetic ordering at the two-dimensional limit (10.1002/advs.202302444), with FM ground state for monolayer CGT, CST, and CSS (10.1016/j.physb.2024.416721). It is a van der Waals ferromagnet (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.014201) and semiconducting ferromagnetic material (10.1103/PhysRevB.100.054420). Interfacial charge injection and lattice mismatch jointly determine Curie temperature (Tc) of heterostructures (10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.094414). Moderate in-plane strain strongly enhances ferromagnetism in Cr2Ge2Te6 up to room temperature (10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.L022040). Cr₂Ge₂Te₆ is a magnetic semiconductor with T_C1 ≈ 69 K (10.1002/smll.202302240), with bipolar tunable magnetization loops below Curie temperature (10.1038/s41565-018-0186-z). Ferromagnetic (FM) Ni (10.1016/j.carbon.2017.05.068), half-metallic ferromagnetic CrO2 (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.104428), ferromagnetic Ni (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.104428), and ferromagnetic nature of Ni (10.1088/2053-1583/aa5a99) are noted. A monolayer of CrI3 is a ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1088/2053-1583/ab8268), and the system is a heterostructure of ferromagnetic monolayer CrCl₃ (10.1038/s41535-025-00759-2). F'1 provides principal stabilization of 2D FM (10.1103/nmyk-mbzz). Ferromagnetic order observed down to monolayer (10.1039/d0tc01322f), monolayer ferromagnet CrI3 (10.1038/s41699-025-00650-5), and the material is a ferromagnetic semiconductor (10.1038/s41563-022-01354-7). Ferromagnetic order with out-of-plane easy axis in monolayer CrI₃ (10.1016/j.commatsci.2020.109820), compressive strain turns system ferromagnetic (10.1088/2053-1583/ab8268). CrI3 monolayer exhibits long-range FM order with Tc ~45 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858), emergence of FM order in monolayers (10.1038/s41565-019-0598-4), monolayer CrI₃ exhibits ferromagnetic order below 45 K (10.1088/2053-1583/aaf06d). Li adsorption dramatically enhances ferromagnetism (10.1016/j.physleta.2020.126754). Magnetic exchange energy increases with reduced interlayer gap, making Tc up to 128.8 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858). A CrI3 monolayer is a 2D FM semiconductor with Curie temperature of 45 K (10.1039/d2nr05342j). External electric field enhances heterostructure FM coupling, with Tc reaching 93.14 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858). CrI₃ is a ferromagnetic monolayer (10.1103/PhysRevB.111.134421), with ferromagnetic order in monolayer reported with Curie temperature of 45 K (10.1088/2053-1583/aa75ed), possessing FM nature of out-of-plane Ising spin-up electrons (10.1016/j.mtadv.2024.100525). The material exhibits ferromagnetic order in pristine state (10.1021/acs.chemmater.9b04645). FM coupling of CrI3 layer in heterostructure enhanced with Tc up to 62.3 K (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149858). Estimation of Curie temperature in monolayer CrI₃ yields 55-65 K (10.1088/2053-1583/ab72d8). Monolayer CrI₃ is a prototypical vdW ferromagnet with isotropic exchange interactions (10.1088/2053-1583/ae1512). FM Fe/Co ultrathin films (10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.149215), single ferromagnetic monolayer (ML) of Fe (10.1088/1367-2630/ab2487), ferromagnetic order detected at 2.35 monolayer Fe film thickness (10.1103/PhysRevB.95.064404), ferromagnetic substrate (10.1016/j.apsusc.2019.144213), ferromagnetic Fe(001) substrate (10.1021/acsanm.5c02678), spin alignment in FGT (10.1016/j.mser.2024.100856). Two-dimensional vdW magnets attract attention (10.1038/s41427-022-00418-z), entering ferromagnetic state at T-c ~200 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.102.161109). Van der Waals 2D ferromagnets provide new way for spintronic devices (10.1021/acsanm.3c05106). Ferromagnetic vdW materials garner attention for excellent magnetic properties (10.1088/2053-1583/ac9dab). raw.name: Co3Sn2S2
raw.text: Co3Sn2S2 is a layered magnetic Weyl semimetal and kagome ferromagnet, also described as a type-I Weyl metal, a half-metallic ferromagnetic kagome compound, a metallic kagome material, a non-layered kagome ferromagnetic material, a 3d transition-metal-based kagome system, a shandite compound with layered kagome-lattices, and a bulk phase known as a topological quasi-2D semimetal in the half-metallic ferromagnetic state (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.115106, 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.085203, 10.1038/s43246-021-00122-5, 10.1038/s41427-023-00525-5, 10.1038/s42005-024-01534-8, 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.214204, 10.7566/JPSJ.85.064706, 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.161301, 10.1002/adma.202509261, 10.1021/accountsmr.3c00291, 10.1038/s42005-021-00627-y, 10.1038/s41567-018-0234-5, 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6, 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.085112, 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.104421, 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.165127, 10.1039/d4tc04933k, 10.1021/acsaelm.9b00650, 10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c02962). The material exhibits long-range out-of-plane ferromagnetic order, with ferromagnetic ordering appearing robustly even in average thicknesses of one or two unit cells, and stabilises a ferromagnetic state similar to the bulk (source: 10.1038/s41567-018-0234-5, 10.1038/s42005-021-00627-y, 10.1038/s42005-024-01534-8, 10.1038/s43246-021-00122-5, 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6). The Curie temperature (Tc) is estimated via a semi-classical Heisenberg model, and a low-field anomalous magnetic phase just below Tc with split zero-field-cooled and field-cooled magnetization curves is explained by temperature-dependent domain wall motion including domain wall creep (source: 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6, 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.3.104421). The material features a large anomalous Hall conductivity (1,130 Omega(-1) cm(-1)) and anomalous Hall angle (20%) in its three-dimensional bulk, and shows a large anomalous Hall effect associated with Weyl nodes, with contributions from X and tlf diagrams cancelling the majority of the noncrossing diagram contribution in tilted Weyl metals (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.115106, 10.1038/s41567-018-0234-5, 10.1038/s42005-024-01534-8, 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.214204). The nodal lines can be fully gapped to quasi-two-dimensional massive Dirac fermions, and massive Dirac or Weyl fermions exist near the Fermi level (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.035107, 10.1021/accountsmr.3c00291). Dispersive spin excitations are observed in both in-plane and out-of-plane directions in the ferromagnetic state, but are damped in the paramagnetic state (source: 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6). The material has low carrier density, and a negative magnetoresistance consistent with the chiral anomaly is observed, along with chiral-anomaly-induced and chirality-dependent magnetoresistance in resistivity analysis (source: 10.1038/s41567-018-0234-5, 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.085203). The Co-based shandites exhibit quasi-two-dimensional itinerant electron magnetism, and the material is a three-dimensional correlated system with a large spin stiffness (source: 10.7566/JPSJ.85.064706, 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6). The estimated magnetic anisotropy energy is approximately 0.6 meV, and a full spin wave gap below Eg = 2.3 meV is observed at T = 4 K (source: 10.1007/s11433-020-1597-6). In weakly and moderately correlated regimes, magnetic correlations remain short-range with no tendencies toward magnetic ordering (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.165127). The material is predicted to realize the quantum anomalous Hall effect in a two-dimensional limit and is ideal for realizing anomalous transport properties based on Berry curvature in specific electronic bands (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.161301, 10.1021/acsaelm.9b00650, 10.1038/s42005-021-00627-y).

raw.text: CoFe2O4 (CFO) is a ternary ferrite (10.1039/d5tc01923k) that exists as a ferrimagnetic solid phase cobalt ferrite (10.1016/j.jpcs.2022.110797), appearing in multiple forms including zero-dimensional nanoparticles (10.1016/j.mtphys.2023.101277), epitaxial thin films (10.1021/acsnano.7b02637), vertically grown nanosheets (10.1021/acsanm.3c05478), ferromagnetic dielectric thin films (10.1021/acsnano.7b02253), and as a 2D ferrimagnetic material component in nanocomposites (10.1002/advs.202303692). It is also used as a ferrimagnetic insulator substrate (10.1088/2053-1583/aa6663) and proposed to induce magnetic correlations in graphene (10.1088/1367-2630/abfd00), and is a ferrimagnetic oxide in multiferroic heterostructures (10.1021/acsami.8b09499) and a magnetic ferrite film (10.1002/adma.202509037). The material exhibits bulklike ferrimagnetism for 5-15 nm thick CFO layers as determined by X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (10.1021/acsami.8b09499). Both the saturation magnetization and coercivity of transferred films can be changed over the bending status (10.1021/acsnano.7b02637).

raw.text: BaTiO3 (barium titanate) is a transition-metal perovskite oxide material, specifically a ferroelectric perovskite, that serves as a ferroelectric component in multiferroic bilayer films (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2025.164591), a ferroelectric oxide in multiferroic heterostructures (source: 10.1021/acsami.8b09499), a ferroelectric perovskite material used as a spacer layer (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2018.03.045), a perovskite oxide used as a superlattice component (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.184417), a ferroelectric material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.155106), a matrix material for ultrathin films (source: 10.3390/nano14070586), a 2D ferroelectric material component in nanocomposites (source: 10.1002/advs.202303692), and a ferroelectric film material (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.034408). It is also described as a quasi-two-dimensional BaTiO3 (001) ultrathin film (source: 10.1016/j.surfin.2025.106759), a two-dimensional BaTiO3 (001) ultrathin film (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.154240), a two-dimensional ultrathin film (source: 10.1063/5.0223008), and an epitaxial ferroelectric BaTiO3 perovskite thin film (source: 10.1021/acsanm.9b01970). Exhibited properties include ferroelectricity, where the switching of the BTO ferroelectric polarization is found dependent on the CFO thickness as measured by piezoresponse force microscopy (source: 10.1021/acsami.8b09499); a diode-like rectifying effect modulated by electric polarization, observed in Al/BTO/LSMO/LNO and Al/LSMO/BTO/LNO devices (source: 10.1016/j.physleta.2025.130696); orbital selective charge transfer occurring on the surprisingly robust two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.155106); and a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) that forms along the domain wall (source: 10.1103/y87v-34d8).

raw.name: EuMg2Sb2
raw.text: EuMg2Sb2 (mat_10_1103_PhysRevB_106_024418_1) is a layered Zintl-phase material that crystallizes in the trigonal CaAl2Si2 crystal structure. It undergoes antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering at the Néel temperature T-N = 8.0(2) K, as determined by magnetic susceptibility and zero-field heat capacity measurements (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418). The AFM order is of A-type, where Eu spins within ab-plane layers are aligned ferromagnetically, while Eu spins in adjacent layers are aligned antiferromagnetically (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418). Below T-N and at low fields of < 0.05 T, very weak in-plane magnetic anisotropy is evident (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418). Additionally, the compound exhibits semiconducting behavior with an activated conductivity at high temperatures, indicating a semiconducting electronic ground state with a narrow energy gap of 370 meV, as measured by electrical resistivity and ARPES (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418).

raw.text: Layered trigonal EuMg2Bi2 is a topological semimetal and isostructural semimetallic compound to EuMg2Sb2 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.024408; 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418). It exhibits A-type antiferromagnetism below the Néel temperature, where adjacent layers are aligned antiferromagnetically (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.024408). The intraplane ordering is ferromagnetic (Eu2+, S = 7/2) with the moments aligned in the ab plane (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.024408). Additionally, EuMg2Bi2 hosts Dirac surface states (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.024418).

raw.name: AlN
raw.text: AlN (aluminum nitride) is a IIIA-nitride binary compound and an ultrawide bandgap semiconductor with a wurtzite structure (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.184427). It exists in multiple forms: bulk and two-dimensional (2D) AlN (source: 10.3389/fphy.2022.843352), including two-dimensional AlN nanosheets (AlNNSs) (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2016.07.024), pristine aluminium nitride nanosheets (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.155803), a semiconducting monolayer material (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2017.08.050), a monolayer material studied for electronic structure and magnetism (source: 10.1016/j.physb.2023.415553), single-layer AlN (source: 10.1088/1402-4896/ab93a7) which can be obtained by chemical vapor deposition and molecular beam epitaxy (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2022.154506), a two-dimensional material prepared by chemical vapor deposition (source: 10.1016/j.apsusc.2023.157831), a tetragonal aluminum nitride monolayer (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2021.110413), a bilayer of AlN (source: 10.1021/acsnano.7b02756), and a fully hydrogenated bilayer aluminum nitride (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.134412). It also serves as a component of AlN/GaN hybrid heterojunctions (source: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2020.109860), an ultrathin AlN layer at the hetero-interface (source: 10.1002/adfm.202009771), a substrate material for epitaxial growth (source: 10.1002/lpor.202500823), and a component of Pt/Co/AlN stacks (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2022.165514). Regarding electronic properties, the conduction-band bottom exhibits s-type symmetry (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.184427), and the valence-band top has p-orbital character (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.184427). For spin-related properties, the Schottky barrier in the UWBG semiconductor AlN acts as a spin filter, increasing the polarization of the spin current injected from the ferromagnet (source: 10.1002/adom.202201535).

raw.name: Ca2RuO4
raw.text: Ca2RuO4 is a calcium-based ruthenate of the Ruddlesden-Popper family (source: 10.1039/d4nr04053h), a transition-metal oxide (source: 10.1103/stt1-v24p), and a layered ruthenate with strong correlations between lattice, spin, and charge degrees of freedom (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074408). It is a quasi-two-dimensional Mott insulator (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.137204) with quasi-two-dimensional antiferromagnetic order (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.067201), described as a condensate of low-lying spin-orbit excitons with angular momentum J(eff) = 1 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.067201), and is a single-layer square-lattice antiferromagnet (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.023181). The material exhibits antiferromagnetic order with Neel temperature T-N (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.023181), collinear antiferromagnetism (source: 10.1038/s41524-023-01025-4), and a metal-insulator transition evolving from an insulating state into a metallic state and then towards an exotic Mott insulator (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074408). It also exhibits orbital ordering (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074408), a metamagnetic transition from a canted antiferromagnetic to a nearly ferromagnetic state (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074408), and an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.074408). The material hosts an altermagnetic Weyl semimetal phase (predicted existence, source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03191), an AFM Weyl semimetal state (source: 10.1038/s41524-023-01025-4), and robust second-order topological states with spin-resolved corner modes (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03191). Spin-wave spectra directly reveal a well-defined, dispersive Higgs mode (source: 10.1038/NPHYS4077), and the amplitude (Higgs) mode of the spin-orbit condensate is observed in A(g) polarization geometry (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.067201). In B-1g geometry, a single-magnon peak as well as two-magnon and two-Higgs excitations are observed (source: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.067201). Critical behavior is characterized by exponents beta (magnetic order parameter M), gamma (susceptibility chi), nu (correlation length xi), and z (characteristic energy Gamma) (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.023181). Note: Some descriptions (e.g., "atomically thin metal oxide phase with composition MO for transition metal element Cr", "monolayer CrO", "2D intrinsic altermagnet candidate", "bulk CrO from which the monolayer is exfoliated") appear to refer to a different material (CrO) and are not merged into the Ca2RuO4 description.

raw.text: Fully halogenated germanene, GeI, is investigated as a model system (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.93.121106). For this material, the frequency-dependent spin Hall conductivity is calculated for two-dimensional atomically thin crystals and one-dimensional nanoribbons; quantization of the static spin Hall conductivity is demonstrated for topological insulators, and the static spin Hall conductivity is hardly influenced by temperature and Fermi level shift, while the frequency dependence of spin Hall conductivity is governed by band-structure details, and topological edge states influence the conductivity mainly for vanishing frequencies (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.93.121106).

content.text: Fermi-arc antiferromagnet

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: NdBi
raw.text: NdBi is a Fermi-arc antiferromagnet (source: 10.1002/advs.202303978) that exhibits Dirac surface states (SSs) with 2-dimensionality and nonzero Berry phase (source: 10.1002/advs.202303978); the orbital magnetic moment of Nd plays a crucial role in fostering these peculiar surface states (source: 10.1002/advs.202303978). Shubnikov–de Haas (SdH) oscillations are successfully verified from the Dirac surface states with 2-dimensionality and nonzero Berry phase (source: 10.1002/advs.202303978). Additionally, a spin-flop transition appears only when the external magnetic field is applied along the [001] direction and features obvious hysteresis for the first time in NdBi (source: 10.1002/advs.202303978).

content.text: two-dimensional material with twisted bilayer structure at specific twist angle

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: magic-angle graphene
raw.text: Magic-angle graphene is a two-dimensional material with a twisted bilayer structure at a specific twist angle (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.235157). It exhibits an intervalley coherent insulator state that spontaneously breaks emergent U(1) valley-charge conservation symmetry and emergent SU(2) symmetry (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.235157). Additionally, it exhibits spin-triplet superconductivity, where the SU(2) Goldstone modes generate a ferromagnetic interaction attractive in spin-triplet pairing channels, with the leading superconducting instability in the p-wave channel as determined by weak-coupling BCS calculation (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.106.235157).

content.text: oxyhalide in the botallackite structure
quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet

raw.label: MaterialSystem
raw.name: Cu2(OH)3Br
raw.text: Cu2(OH)3Br is an oxyhalide in the botallackite structure and a quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet, consisting of Cu2+ S = 1/2 moments arranged on a distorted triangular lattice (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.024407). It exhibits antiferromagnetic ordering with ordered spins below TN = 9.3 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.L100405). A field-induced phase transition from the 3D ordered to a disordered phase occurs at Bc = 16.3 T (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.L100405). The system is featured by an onset of a one-half plateaulike magnetization, and magnetization saturation occurs with full symmetry restoration at a much higher field of Bs ≈ 95 T (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.L100405). Exact diagonalization calculations generate magnetic spectral functions consistent with inelastic neutron scattering data (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.024407).

raw.text: VS2 (mat_10_1088_1367-2630_18_11_113038_1) is a material system that exhibits ferromagnetism. Monolayer VS2 exhibits strong ferromagnetic ordering with a saturation magnetization strength (M-s) of 37 emu per cc and a coercivity (H-c) of 135 Oe at 300 K (source: 10.1002/adfm.202213295). Monolayer VS2 and VSe2 are ferromagnetic (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/18/11/113038). Magnetic force microscopy measurements suggest room-temperature ferromagnetism in ultrathin VS₂ flakes (source: 10.1021/acsanm.9b00608). Ferromagnetic pristine VS2 nanosheets are reported (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2017.01.192). Realizing ferromagnetism SOTIs by identifying two real materials, including the 1T-VS2 monolayer (source: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c03109). Coexistence of stable ferromagnetic ordering in VS₂/ZnPSe₃ heterostructure is noted (source: 10.1016/j.physleta.2024.129590).

raw.name: YbOCl
raw.text: YbOCl is a representative member of the van der Waals layered honeycomb rare-earth chalcohalide REChX family (RE = rare earth; Ch = O, S, Se, Te; X = F, Cl, Br, I), which is a newly reported family of Kitaev spin liquid candidates, and YbOCl is the first single crystal of the family grown (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/38/4/047502; 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.033006; 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.033274; 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043061). The Yb3+ ion possesses an effective spin of 1/2 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043061). Magnetic and heat capacity measurements down to 1.8 K find no obvious magnetic transition in YbOCl (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/38/4/047502). The van der Waals interlayer coupling highlights the true two-dimensionality of the family (source: 10.1088/0256-307X/38/4/047502). The family offers a platform where a strong spin-orbit coupling meets a van der Waals layered and undistorted honeycomb spin lattice, which outputs highly anisotropic exchange couplings required by the Kitaev model, with J(±) ≈ -0.3 K and J(zz) ≈ 1.6 K determined via mean-field scenario and self-consistent simulations, and the self-consistent simulations also give g factors of g(ab) ≈ 3.4 and g(c) ≈ 2.9 (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.033006). The phase diagram hosts rich magnetic phases including a spin-disordered one (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.033006). Experiments reveal an antiferromagnetic phase below 1.3 K (T_N = 1.3 K) identified as a spin ground state with an intralayer ferromagnetic and interlayer antiferromagnetic ordering via thermodynamic measurements (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.033274). The crystalline electric field (CEF) excitations in YbOCl were unambiguously identified using polarized Raman spectra, revealing multiple discrete energy levels at 1.8 K, and Raman experiments also reveal anomalous nonlinear CEF splitting under applied magnetic fields (source: 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043061).

raw.name: TaFe1.25Te3
raw.text: TaFe1.25Te3 is a layered antiferromagnet with a spin-ladder structure (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084408). Magnetization studies reveal an anisotropic magnetic behavior resulting in the stabilization of a spin-flop configuration for H perpendicular to the (10-1) plane (i.e., out-of-plane direction) (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084408). A significant anisotropic enhancement of magnetoresistance is observed when H is perpendicular to the (10-1) plane compared to H parallel to the (10-1) directions (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084408). Additionally, angle-dependent longitudinal and transverse magnetoresistances show an unusual anharmonic behavior (source: 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.6.084408).

raw.text: Cr2I3Br3 is a Janus Cr2I3X3 monolayer with X=Br (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778), classified as a Janus magnetic semiconductor van der Waals material (source: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c03349) with a 2D Janus structure exhibiting mechanical and thermodynamic stability (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3). It is an indirect band gap semiconductor (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778) and also shows indirect-gap semiconductor behavior (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3). The material possesses good stability, intrinsic ferromagnetism (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778), and ferromagnetic ordering (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3). It is a half semiconductor with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778) and exhibits electric polarization (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778), with intrinsic vertical electric polarity (EP) investigated by surface potential difference analysis and dipole calculations (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3).

raw.text: The Janus Cr2I3Cl3 monolayer (X=Cl) is a 2D structure with mechanical and thermodynamic stability (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3). It is a bipolar magnetic semiconductor with in-plane magnetic anisotropy (IMA) (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778). As part of the Janus Cr2I3X3 monolayers, it is an indirect band gap semiconductor with good stability, intrinsic ferromagnetism, and electric polarization (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900778). Additionally, Janus Cr2I3Y3 monolayers (where Y includes Cl) show indirect-gap semiconductors with ferromagnetic ordering and intrinsic vertical electric polarity (EP), as investigated by surface potential difference analysis and dipole calculations (source: 10.1038/s41699-022-00343-3).

raw.name: CrX2
raw.text: CrX2 (X = S, Se, Te, Cl, Br, I) is a two-dimensional (2D) layered van der Waals magnetic material, also described as a transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) with magnetic transition metal element Cr, existing in monolayer, bilayer, and bulk forms with orthorhombic, trigonal, 1T, 2H, or 2H crystal phases. It exhibits half-metallicity, with Cr2Se3 being a half-metallic 2D material; planar Cr2S3 and Cr2Se3 are ferromagnetic half-metals with mirror-symmetry-protected nodal lines for the spin-down channel and a large direct gap for the spin-up channel (source: 10.1002/aelm.201900490). VX2, CrX2, and MnX2 chains can be converted to half metals via carrier doping (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c). MX2 is a ferromagnetic (FM) half-metal material with a large spin and a half-metallic gap (source: 10.1016/j.rinp.2023.106687). Both structures have half metallicity (source: 10.1016/j.jpcs.2023.111805). Many screened 2D FM materials are half-metals, hosting 100% spin polarization ratio (source: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2024.178059). dLieb-MSe2 (M = Nb, V, Cr) exhibits half-metallicity (source: 10.1103/m9xb-sprm). The half-metallic characteristic is retained in Cr2Se3/Sb, Cr2Se3/MoTe2, Cr2Se3/WTe2, Cr2Se3/WSeTe-Se, and Cr2Se3/WSeTe-Te interfaces (source: 10.1021/acsami.4c13805). It shows ferromagnetism; the magnetic ground state transforms to a ferromagnetic state upon hydrogenation, with an estimated ferromagnetic transition temperature of the CrS2-2H monolayer of 310 K, which can be enhanced to 430 K under a compressive strain of -4% (source: 10.1103/slw3-nmn4). It exhibits a nonzero Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), with a small DMI energy that changes sign with ferroelectric polarization switching, and the DMI and polarization are enhanced to 0.28 meV/formula-unit when Pt intercalates bilayers of CrI2 (method: DFT calculation; source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094435). The ground state of bulk CrI2 has an electric polarization of 0.15 μC/cm² pointing along the z-axis, enhanced to 0.63 μC/cm² when Pt intercalates bilayers of CrI2 (method: DFT calculation; source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.094435). It shows actuation strain output, inducing a phase transition between two charge density wave (CDW) states in CrS2, leading to significant actuation strain output of 12.17% along the x direction and 5.93% along the y direction (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.024414). A ferroelectric switching pathway driven by interlayer sliding is predicted, featuring a low switching energy barrier and out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01912-y). CrI2 is a van der Waals layered material that exhibits helimagnetism that propagates along ribbon chains, with a Néel temperature T-N = 17 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.144403). MX2 atomic chains are lattice-dynamically stable, confirmed from phonon spectra and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c). Monte Carlo simulations based on DFT-calculated magnetic exchange interactions suggest a proper-screw helimagnetic ground state with a Néel temperature consistent with experimental observations (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01912-y). The RKKY interaction is nearly independent of the lattice size in a reasonably large range and the number of CrS2 layers (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L041401). Below T-N = 17 K in the orthorhombic structure, a screwlike helimagnetic order develops with an incommensurate wave vector of q ≈ (0.2492, 0, 0) at 8 K (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.109.144403). The extracted spin-driven polarization aligns along the z-axis (source: 10.1038/s41524-025-01912-y). Both 2D materials are found to be structurally stable under ambient conditions (source: 10.1002/adfm.202500907). It shows large valley spin splitting in the valence band (source: 10.1088/1367-2630/ab7256). It exhibits bipolar magnetic semiconducting characteristics (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.205407). CrX2 chains are bipolar magnetic (source: 10.1039/d2na00543c). It shows a drastic change of magnetism (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.024414). It exhibits a ferromagnetic charge density wave state, with a few ferromagnetic (FM) cases of TMDs CDW states (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.024414). In-plane magnetic orders of CrS2 mono and few layers are tunable between striped antiferromagnetic (sAFM) and ferromagnetic (FM) orders (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.245409). It exhibits high-Curie-temperature (TC) Ising ferromagnetism (source: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.205407).

raw.text: α-RuCl₃ is a layered honeycomb antiferromagnet and van der Waals material (10.1103/PhysRevB.98.094425; 10.1016/j.aop.2026.170393; 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.045419) that is a prime candidate for realizing a Kitaev quantum spin liquid (10.1002/admi.202200754; 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.094410; 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.206501; 10.1039/d2nr02827a; 10.1038/s41563-022-01401-3; 10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.8.014402; 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L041112; 10.1103/PhysRevX.12.021025; 10.1063/5.0101512). It is a spin-orbit coupled Mott insulator (10.1103/PhysRevB.111.184440; 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.104425; 10.1103/PhysRevB.102.155134; 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.214413; 10.1103/zbbd-dqzb; 10.1103/nbfx-x8f6; 10.1021/acsnano.4c06937; 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.165134) with a quasi-two-dimensional honeycomb lattice of edge-sharing octahedra (10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.037202; 10.1103/PhysRevB.98.100403; 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155124). The optimized 3D structure without electronic correlations has P3̄1m space-group symmetry independent of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), but including electronic correlation changes the optimized 3D structure to either C2/m or Cmc2₁ within 0.1 meV per formula unit energy difference (10.1103/PhysRevB.93.155143). SOC suppresses dimerization of Ru atoms, making the honeycomb closer to an ideal one (10.1103/PhysRevB.93.155143). The material exhibits antiferromagnetic order below 10 K (10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b01691), with a transition to a state with antiferromagnetic order below TN ≈ 7 K (10.1103/PhysRevX.12.021025) and a Néel temperature below 15 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.95.241112). The antiferromagnetic order at 7-13 K in pristine α-RuCl₃ is successfully suppressed down to 2 K in bilayer hydrated LiₓRuCl₃·yH₂O (10.1103/PhysRevB.99.245141). The low-temperature antiferromagnetic ordered phase features a broad Raman continuum (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.140410). Pressure-induced melting of antiferromagnetic order occurs at a critical pressure below 1 GPa (10.1103/PhysRevB.97.245149). In zero field, the material orders magnetically below 7 K with zigzag order within the honeycomb planes (10.1103/PhysRevB.95.180411), and this zero-field zigzag phase is detected in the zigzag ordered phase (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.174444; 10.1103/PhysRevB.96.241107). The third nearest neighbor antiferromagnetic Heisenberg interaction J₃ stabilizes the zigzag antiferromagnetic order (10.1103/PhysRevB.96.054410), which undergoes a transition at TN = 34 K (10.1103/PhysRevB.105.L041112) and is suppressed by an applied magnetic field (10.1103/PhysRevB.110.L241109). The spin liquid whose spinon condensation leads to the zigzag magnetic order was observed in Na₂IrO₃ and α-RuCl₃ (10.1103/PhysRevB.99.205119). At moderate magnetic field strength parallel to the zigzag axis, there is growing evidence for a quantum spin-liquid state (10.1038/s41567-021-01243-x), with a putative spin liquid phase in the paramagnetic state at high magnetic fields (10.1038/s41567-021-01488-6). Single-layer α-RuCl₃ has been proposed as a potential quantum spin liquid (10.1103/PhysRevB.108.064401), and the material hosts a proximate quantum spin-liquid state (10.1016/j.mtphys.2022.100803). The thermal Hall conductivity κxy of Majorana fermions is predicted to be half-quantized (10.1038/s41563-022-01397-w), with positive κxy developing gradually upon cooling below T ~ 80 K (10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.217205). The plateau-like behavior of the half-quantized thermal Hall conductivity as a function of external magnetic field, and the sign change depending on the magnetic field orientations, have been proposed as strong evidence for the non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid (10.1103/PhysRevB.103.174402). κxy/T is strongly temperature dependent between 0.5 and 10 K (10.1038/s41563-022-01397-w), and model-dependent behavior in both magnitude and sign of κxy with temperature-dependent sign reversals is observed in certain instances (10.1016/j.aop.2026.170393). The heat capacity exhibits a characteristic two-peak structure in external magnetic fields far beyond quantum criticality, with excess heat capacity existing at temperatures well above the onset of magnetic order in zero field (10.1103/PhysRevB.99.094415). The lower peak appears around the onset of magnetic order in zero field and shifts to 10 K at higher fields, while the high-temperature peak located around 70 K carries entropy R/2 ln 2 (10.1103/PhysRevB.99.094415). The SPC induced heat capacity is also analyzed (10.1039/d0nr08626f). Oscillations in the field dependence of the thermal conductivity are observed for an in-plane magnetic field B up to a critical field B*, with periodic oscillations of very large amplitude within the moderate field range and strongly suppressed on either side (10.1038/s41567-021-01243-x; 10.1103/PhysRevB.107.064408). Two magnon-like excitations are observed at 2.7 and 3.6 meV via Raman spectroscopy (10.1103/PhysRevB.101.140410). Two pronounced peaks at A1 = 249 meV and A2 = 454 meV are assigned to single and double spin-orbit excitons, respectively, via Raman spectroscopy (10.1038/s41535-021-00340-7), and both RuX₃ compounds commonly feature single and double spin-orbit excitons of almost identical energies (10.1103/PhysRevB.106.174430). Ferromagnetism is reported with Tc = 89 K from Monte Carlo simulation (10.1016/j.mtphys.2022.100803).
